chunks.title: AWS Certificate Manager: public/private certs and renewal
chunks.text:
AWS Certificate Manager: public/private certs and renewal. AWS Certificate Manager (ACM) provides public and private TLS certificates for integrated AWS services and manages renewal of eligible Amazon-issued certificates. Choose an ACM-issued certificate when managed renewal matters; if a required certificate is imported, plan to monitor its expiration and replace it yourself.
When to use: An application needs a TLS certificate for an integrated service such as Elastic Load Balancing or CloudFront.; A team wants eligible Amazon-issued certificates renewed automatically through DNS validation.; A third-party certificate must be imported, so the team needs an expiration and replacement process.
Key facts: ACM-issued public and private certificates can receive managed renewal; with DNS validation, ACM renews eligible certificates automatically.; Imported certificates are not eligible for ACM managed renewal, even when associated with an AWS service.; ACM certificates are regional. An Elastic Load Balancing deployment in multiple Regions needs a certificate in each Region, with domain validation in each Region for ACM-issued certificates.; A certificate used with CloudFront must be requested or imported in US East (N. Virginia).; When ACM renews a certificate, its ARN remains the same.
Gotchas: Importing a third-party certificate into ACM does not make it eligible for managed renewal.; An ACM certificate in another Region cannot be copied to serve a second regional load balancer.; A private certificate issued directly through the AWS Private CA IssueCertificate API is not eligible for ACM managed renewal.; ACME-issued certificates are renewed by the ACME client, not by ACM managed renewal.
Confused with: 
ES: AWS Certificate Manager (ACM) proporciona certificados TLS públicos y privados para servicios de AWS integrados y gestiona la renovación de certificados elegibles emitidos por Amazon. Si necesitas managed renewal, elige un certificado emitido mediante ACM; si debes importar uno, planifica cómo supervisar su vencimiento y reemplazarlo. Los certificados públicos y privados emitidos mediante ACM pueden recibir managed renewal; con DNS validation, ACM renueva automáticamente los certificados elegibles.; Los certificados importados no son elegibles para ACM managed renewal, aunque estén asociados con un servicio de AWS.; Los certificados de ACM son recursos regionales. Si usas Elastic Load Balancing en varias regiones, necesitas un certificado en cada una y debes validar los dominios en cada región para certificados emitidos mediante ACM.; Un certificado para CloudFront debe solicitarse o importarse en US East (N. Virginia).; Cuando ACM renueva un certificado, su ARN no cambia.

chunks.title: AWS Certificate Manager: public/private certs and renewal
chunks.text:
Scenario: A travel publisher is launching a public website through a CloudFront distribution. The team controls the domain's DNS records and wants an eligible certificate to renew automatically without tracking expiration dates. Which solution meets these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?
Correct: Request a DNS-validated ACM public certificate in US East (N. Virginia), and associate it with CloudFront.
Why: The deciding requirements are CloudFront use and automatic renewal with minimal certificate maintenance. CloudFront requires its ACM certificate in US East (N. Virginia), and ACM automatically renews eligible Amazon-issued certificates that use DNS validation. Putting an ACM certificate in the origin's Region misses CloudFront's certificate Region requirement. Importing a third-party certificate also misses the renewal requirement because imported certificates are not eligible for ACM managed renewal.
Wrong options: Import a third-party certificate into ACM in US East (N. Virginia), and rely on ACM to renew it. (The Region is correct, but imported certificates are not eligible for ACM managed renewal.); Request a DNS-validated ACM public certificate in the Region where the website's origin runs, and associate it with CloudFront. (A CloudFront certificate must be requested or imported in US East (N. Virginia), regardless of the origin's Region.); Use an ACME client to obtain a public certificate for the origin server, and rely on ACM to renew it for CloudFront. (ACME client-managed renewal is not ACM managed renewal and does not provide the requested ACM certificate for CloudFront.)

chunks.title: AWS Certificate Manager: public/private certs and renewal
chunks.text:
Scenario: A ticketing company is deploying regional load balancers for the same public domain in two AWS Regions. It controls DNS for the domain and wants eligible certificates to renew automatically, while keeping certificate administration as simple as possible. Which two actions meet these requirements? (Choose two.)
Correct: Use DNS validation for both ACM-issued certificates so eligible certificates renew automatically. + Request an ACM public certificate in each load balancer's Region and validate the domain for each certificate.
Why: The company must satisfy both regional certificate placement and automatic renewal. ACM certificates are regional, so it must request and validate an ACM public certificate in each load balancer's Region. DNS validation allows eligible Amazon-issued certificates to renew automatically. A single certificate cannot be copied between Regions, and importing certificates would not provide ACM managed renewal.
Wrong options: Request one ACM public certificate and copy it into the second load balancer's Region. (ACM certificates cannot be copied between Regions.); Request one ACM public certificate in US East (N. Virginia) and use it with both regional load balancers. (The US East (N. Virginia) requirement applies to CloudFront; regional load balancers need certificates in their respective Regions.); Import a third-party certificate into each Region and rely on ACM managed renewal for both copies. (Regional imports would address placement, but imported certificates are not eligible for ACM managed renewal.)

chunks.title: AI services for language and speech: Comprehend, Translate, Lex, Polly, Transcribe
chunks.text:
AI services for language and speech: Comprehend, Translate, Lex, Polly, Transcribe. Choose the managed AI service by the input and desired output: Comprehend analyzes text, Translate changes its language, Lex builds chatbots, Polly turns text into speech, and Transcribe turns speech into text. When a service already performs the required task, it avoids building a custom model.
When to use: Analyze sentiment, entities, or PII in existing text: Amazon Comprehend.; Translate text into another language or build a conversational chatbot: Amazon Translate or Amazon Lex, respectively.; Produce spoken audio from text or obtain text from audio: Amazon Polly or Amazon Transcribe, respectively.
Key facts: Amazon Comprehend provides pre-trained analysis of text for entities, key phrases, PII, language, and sentiment.; Amazon Comprehend supports real-time analysis for small workloads and asynchronous jobs for large document sets.; Amazon Polly converts text to speech; generated speech can be cached and replayed.; Amazon Transcribe converts audio to text using streaming transcription or batch transcription of media files in Amazon S3.; Amazon Lex is for chatbots; Amazon Translate is for language translation.
Gotchas: Polly and Transcribe handle opposite directions of speech conversion.; Detecting the language or sentiment of text with Comprehend does not translate it.; Extracting text from a scanned document with Textract is different from analyzing the meaning or PII of text with Comprehend.; Do not choose a custom model in SageMaker AI when a purpose-built service meets the stated requirement.
Confused with: ai-vision-document-services: Textract extracts text, forms, and tables from documents; Rekognition analyzes images or video, rather than providing the requested language or speech function.; sagemaker-ai: SageMaker AI is for building, training, and deploying custom models when a purpose-built service does not fit.
ES: Elige el servicio de AI administrado según la entrada y la salida deseada: Comprehend analiza texto, Translate cambia su idioma, Lex crea chatbots, Polly convierte texto en voz y Transcribe convierte voz en texto. Si un servicio ya realiza la tarea, evitas crear un modelo personalizado. Amazon Comprehend ofrece análisis preentrenado de texto para entidades, frases clave, PII, idioma y sentimiento.; Amazon Comprehend admite análisis en tiempo real para cargas pequeñas y trabajos asíncronos para grandes conjuntos de documentos.; Amazon Polly convierte texto en voz; puedes guardar en caché y reproducir el audio generado.; Amazon Transcribe convierte audio en texto mediante transcripción streaming o transcripción batch de archivos multimedia en Amazon S3.; Amazon Lex sirve para chatbots; Amazon Translate sirve para traducir idiomas.

chunks.title: AI services for language and speech: Comprehend, Translate, Lex, Polly, Transcribe
chunks.text:
Scenario: A property-management company receives thousands of tenant messages as text. Before analysts review them, the company wants to identify messages containing personally identifiable information and measure overall sentiment. It does not want to develop a machine learning model. Which solution meets these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?
Correct: Use Amazon Comprehend to analyze each message for PII and sentiment.
Why: The input is already text, and the required outputs are PII identification and sentiment. Amazon Comprehend provides both capabilities through pre-trained text analysis, so the company need not develop a model. Amazon Textract would address extraction from documents, not analysis of these existing text messages; SageMaker AI would add unnecessary model-building work.
Wrong options: Build and deploy a custom text-analysis model with Amazon SageMaker AI. (A custom model adds development work when Comprehend already supports the required analyses.); Use Amazon Textract to extract text from each message. (The messages are already text, and text extraction does not provide the requested PII and sentiment analysis.); Use Amazon Translate to process each message before analysts review it. (Translate changes the language of text but does not provide the requested PII and sentiment analysis.)

chunks.title: AI services for language and speech: Comprehend, Translate, Lex, Polly, Transcribe
chunks.text:
Scenario: An international logistics company stores recorded driver interviews as audio files in Amazon S3. Reviewers need written transcripts of the recordings and then need the transcript text translated into another language. The company wants purpose-built managed services instead of developing models. Which TWO services meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead? (Choose two.)
Correct: Amazon Transcribe, to convert the stored audio files into text + Amazon Translate, to convert the transcript text into another language
Why: The workflow has two distinct transformations: recorded audio to written text, then text into another language. Amazon Transcribe can transcribe media files stored in Amazon S3, and Amazon Translate addresses the translation requirement. Comprehend can detect a text's language but does not translate it; Polly converts text in the opposite direction, into speech.
Wrong options: Amazon Polly, to synthesize speech from the transcripts (Polly converts text to audio, which is not one of the requested outputs.); Amazon Textract, to extract text from the stored audio files (Textract extracts information from documents, not speech from audio files.); Amazon Comprehend, to detect the language and sentiment of the transcripts (Detecting language or sentiment does not produce transcripts or translate them.)

chunks.title: AI services for vision and documents: Rekognition and Textract
chunks.text:
AI services for vision and documents: Rekognition and Textract. Choose Amazon Rekognition to analyze visual content in images and videos, such as objects, faces, and unsafe content. Choose Amazon Textract when the goal is to extract text or structured information from documents, especially forms and tables.
When to use: Images or videos need object labels, face comparison, or content moderation: use Rekognition.; Scanned documents need typed or handwritten text extracted: use Textract.; A workflow needs fields from forms or cells from document tables: use Textract Document Analysis.
Key facts: Rekognition analyzes images and videos without requiring machine learning expertise.; Rekognition can detect text in images, but Textract provides document-specific analysis of forms and tables.; Textract analyzes image files and PDF files; its Document Analysis API extracts text, forms, and tables.; Textract offers synchronous processing for single-page documents and asynchronous operations for multipage documents.
Gotchas: Do not choose Textract just because a photograph contains text; visual labels, faces, and moderation point to Rekognition.; Do not choose Rekognition text detection when the requirement is to extract form fields or table cells from documents.; Do not choose a text-language service to analyze the visual content of an image.
Confused with: ai-language-services: Language services work with tasks such as sentiment or PII analysis in text; Rekognition analyzes visual content, while Textract extracts content from documents.; sagemaker-ai: SageMaker AI is for building, training, and deploying custom models when a pre-trained service does not fit.
ES: Elige Amazon Rekognition para analizar contenido visual en imágenes y videos, como objetos, rostros y contenido inapropiado. Elige Amazon Textract cuando necesites extraer texto o información estructurada de documentos, especialmente formularios y tablas. Rekognition analiza imágenes y videos sin que necesites experiencia en machine learning.; Rekognition puede detectar texto en imágenes, pero Textract ofrece análisis de formularios y tablas en documentos.; Textract analiza archivos de imagen y PDF; su Document Analysis API extrae texto, formularios y tablas.; Textract ofrece procesamiento síncrono de documentos de una página y operaciones asíncronas para documentos de varias páginas.

chunks.title: AI services for vision and documents: Rekognition and Textract
chunks.text:
Scenario: A community marketplace stores seller-uploaded product photos in Amazon S3. Before publishing each listing, it must detect explicit or violent visual content and flag the affected photos; sellers do not submit documents or audio. Which solution meets these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?
Correct: Use Amazon Rekognition content moderation to analyze the uploaded photos.
Why: The deciding requirement is to flag explicit or violent content in seller photos, not to analyze text or documents. Amazon Rekognition provides unsafe-content detection for images without requiring machine learning expertise. Textract is designed for document extraction, while a custom SageMaker AI model would add work despite an available managed capability.
Wrong options: Train and deploy a custom image moderation model with Amazon SageMaker AI. (A custom model adds model-building work when Rekognition already provides image content moderation.); Use Amazon Comprehend to analyze text detected in the listings. (Text analysis does not determine whether the photos themselves contain unsafe visual content.); Use Amazon Textract Document Analysis to process the uploaded photos. (Textract analyzes document text and structure, not visual categories of unsafe content.)

chunks.title: AI services for vision and documents: Rekognition and Textract
chunks.text:
Scenario: A regional insurer receives scanned, multipage claim packets as PDFs. Its claims system needs the text from completed forms and the cells of attached cost tables so employees no longer retype them. Which solution meets these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?
Correct: Use asynchronous Amazon Textract Document Analysis on the packets.
Why: These PDFs are multipage documents, and the required output includes form information and table cells. Amazon Textract Document Analysis extracts that structured content, and Textract offers asynchronous operations for multipage documents. Rekognition can detect text in images, but that does not satisfy the stated need for document form and table analysis.
Wrong options: Use Amazon Rekognition text detection on images of the packet pages. (Rekognition detects text in images but does not provide the requested document form and table analysis.); Build and host a custom document extraction model with Amazon SageMaker AI. (A custom model adds development and hosting work when Textract provides the required extraction.); Use Amazon Comprehend to identify entities in extracted claim text. (Entity analysis does not extract the form fields and table cells from the scanned PDFs.)

chunks.title: Application Load Balancer: path/host routing, targets, auth
chunks.text:
Application Load Balancer: path/host routing, targets, auth. An Application Load Balancer (ALB) handles HTTP and HTTPS traffic at Layer 7 and uses listener rules to send requests to target groups based on request content. Choose it when a scenario requires routing by path, host, or HTTP header, or needs load-balancer authentication or AWS WAF integration.
When to use: One HTTP/HTTPS entry point must route paths or hostnames to different services.; Container, IP-address, or Lambda targets need application-level routing.; The load balancer must authenticate users before forwarding requests or work with AWS WAF.
Key facts: ALB listeners support HTTP and HTTPS; listener rules are evaluated in priority order, with the default rule performed last.; Rules can match URL paths, host headers, other HTTP headers, methods, query parameters, and source IP addresses.; Target groups can contain EC2 instances, IP addresses, or Lambda functions; container tasks can be registered with a target group.; Health checks are configured per target group, allowing services to be monitored independently.; An HTTPS listener can terminate client encryption at the ALB; AWS WAF can allow or block requests using a web ACL.
Gotchas: A Network Load Balancer (NLB) TCP listener can pass encrypted traffic to targets, but it cannot make decisions from HTTP paths or hosts.; An HTTPS listener on an ALB decrypts client requests; do not choose it when targets must perform the initial decryption.; A listener needs a default rule even when additional path- or host-based rules exist.
Confused with: nlb-static-ip-tcp-udp: Choose NLB for transport-level TCP/UDP needs or TCP pass-through, not HTTP content-based routing.; gateway-load-balancer: Choose Gateway Load Balancer to insert virtual security appliances into traffic flows, not to route web requests among applications.
ES: Un Application Load Balancer (ALB) maneja tráfico HTTP y HTTPS en Layer 7 y usa reglas del listener para enviar solicitudes a target groups según el contenido de cada solicitud. Elígelo cuando necesites enrutar por ruta, host o encabezado HTTP, o cuando el balanceador deba autenticar usuarios o integrarse con AWS WAF. Los listeners de ALB admiten HTTP y HTTPS; evalúan las reglas por prioridad y ejecutan la regla predeterminada al final.; Las reglas pueden evaluar rutas URL, encabezados host, otros encabezados HTTP, métodos, parámetros de consulta y direcciones IP de origen.; Los target groups pueden incluir instancias EC2, direcciones IP o funciones Lambda; las tareas de contenedores también pueden registrarse en un target group.; Configuras las comprobaciones de estado por target group, lo que permite monitorear cada servicio por separado.; Un listener HTTPS puede terminar el cifrado del cliente en el ALB; AWS WAF puede permitir o bloquear solicitudes mediante una web ACL.

chunks.title: Application Load Balancer: path/host routing, targets, auth
chunks.text:
Scenario: A software provider serves two HTTPS applications from separate container services behind one load balancer. Requests with an X-Product header value of alpha must reach the alpha service, and requests with a value of beta must reach the beta service; the provider also wants independent target health checks. Which TWO configuration choices meet these requirements? (Choose two.)
Correct: Create ALB listener rules with HTTP header conditions for the two X-Product values. + Register the services in separate ALB target groups and configure health checks for each group.
Why: The deciding constraints are routing by an HTTP header and checking the two services independently. ALB listener rules can match HTTP headers, and health checks are configured per target group, so separate groups satisfy the health requirement. One shared ALB target group loses that independence; NLB and Gateway Load Balancer do not supply the requested HTTP header routing.
Wrong options: Register both services in one ALB target group and use one health-check configuration. (A shared target group would not provide the requested independent health-check configurations.); Insert both services behind a Gateway Load Balancer and route by the X-Product header. (Gateway Load Balancer is for virtual appliances, not HTTP header-based service routing.); Create NLB listener rules that inspect X-Product and forward to the matching service. (NLB does not provide HTTP header-based listener routing.)

chunks.title: Application Load Balancer: path/host routing, targets, auth
chunks.text:
Scenario: A travel company is retiring a small EC2 service that generates HTTP booking confirmations. It wants requests under /confirm to invoke a Lambda function while requests under /search continue to reach EC2 instances, all through the same HTTPS entry point. Which design meets these requirements?
Correct: Use an ALB with path rules forwarding /confirm to a Lambda target group and /search to an EC2 target group.
Why: The design needs both URL-path decisions and a Lambda target alongside EC2 targets. An ALB supports path conditions and can forward to target groups containing the appropriate target types. A single default action sending everything to Lambda would break /search, while an NLB does not provide the required path-based routing.
Wrong options: Use a Gateway Load Balancer with separate appliance groups for /confirm and /search. (Gateway Load Balancer is not designed to route HTTP paths to Lambda and EC2 applications.); Use an NLB with separate target groups for the Lambda function and EC2 instances. (NLB cannot route requests by URL path or register Lambda as the described target.); Use an ALB with one default action that forwards both paths to the Lambda function. (Sending both paths to Lambda would stop /search from reaching the EC2 instances.)

chunks.title: Amazon ECS: EC2 vs Fargate launch types
chunks.text:
Amazon ECS: EC2 vs Fargate launch types. Amazon ECS orchestrates containers; the capacity choice determines who manages the infrastructure. Choose Fargate when you do not want to manage servers, and ECS on EC2 when you must directly control instances, such as for a custom AMI, privileged capabilities, or capacity reservations.
When to use: Choose Fargate for container workloads with variable demand and minimal infrastructure management.; Choose ECS on EC2 when the team must select, configure, and maintain the underlying instances.; Choose ECS on EC2 for requirements such as custom AMIs, privileged capabilities, or capacity reservations.
Key facts: Fargate is serverless: you pay for the resources tasks use without managing infrastructure.; With ECS on EC2, you manage instance selection, configuration, and maintenance.; An ECS service maintains a desired number of tasks and replaces tasks that stop.; Amazon ECS Managed Instances is a separate capacity option that provides access to EC2 capabilities while AWS manages the underlying instances.
Gotchas: Do not select EC2 merely because an application runs continuously; an ECS service can run on Fargate.; Do not select Fargate when the requirement explicitly calls for a custom AMI or privileged capabilities.; GPU access alone does not prove that the team must manage EC2 instances: ECS Managed Instances also supports GPU acceleration.
Confused with: Amazon ECS Managed Instances: It offers EC2 instance capabilities while AWS handles provisioning, patching, scaling, and maintenance; ECS on EC2 puts instance management on your team.; AWS Fargate: Fargate runs ECS tasks without server management; ECS on EC2 gives your team direct control of the instances.
ES: Amazon ECS orquesta contenedores; la opción de capacidad determina quién administra la infraestructura. Elige Fargate si no quieres administrar servidores y ECS on EC2 si debes controlar directamente las instancias, por ejemplo, para usar una custom AMI, privileged capabilities o capacity reservations. Fargate es serverless: pagas por los recursos que usan las tareas sin administrar infraestructura.; Con ECS on EC2, administras la selección, configuración y el mantenimiento de las instancias.; Un ECS service mantiene el número deseado de tareas y reemplaza las que se detienen.; Amazon ECS Managed Instances es otra opción de capacidad: permite usar capacidades de EC2 mientras AWS administra las instancias subyacentes.

chunks.title: Amazon ECS: EC2 vs Fargate launch types
chunks.text:
Scenario: A ticketing company has packaged its API as a container image. Traffic changes sharply around event announcements, and the team wants an ECS service to maintain the required number of tasks without selecting or maintaining hosts. Which capacity option meets these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?
Correct: Run the ECS service on Fargate.
Why: The deciding constraints are variable traffic and no host selection or maintenance. Fargate is the serverless ECS capacity option and is suited to variable workloads. ECS on EC2 would leave instance selection and maintenance with the team. ECS Managed Instances reduces infrastructure work, but the scenario does not call for its EC2 instance capabilities.
Wrong options: Run the ECS service on ECS Managed Instances. (AWS manages those instances, but Fargate more directly meets the stated requirement to avoid managing or selecting hosts.); Run the ECS service on EC2 instances selected and maintained by the team. (Team-managed EC2 instances add the host selection and maintenance the company wants to avoid.); Register company-operated servers with ECS Anywhere and run the service there. (Company-operated servers do not satisfy the requirement to avoid maintaining hosts.)

chunks.title: Amazon ECS: EC2 vs Fargate launch types
chunks.text:
Scenario: A media company is moving an existing containerized transcoding service to Amazon ECS. Its operations team must launch container hosts from a company-approved custom AMI and perform the host configuration itself. Which capacity option meets these requirements?
Correct: Run the service on team-managed EC2 instances.
Why: The custom AMI and team-performed host configuration decide this choice. ECS on EC2 gives the team direct responsibility for instance configuration and is a documented choice for custom AMIs. Fargate removes host management rather than providing that control. ECS Managed Instances also places underlying instance management with AWS.
Wrong options: Run the service on ECS Managed Instances. (AWS manages the underlying instances, conflicting with the team's requirement to configure the hosts itself.); Run the service on Fargate. (Fargate does not give the team the required control over a custom host AMI.); Register existing on-premises servers with ECS Anywhere. (On-premises servers do not meet the requirement to launch container hosts from the specified AMI in AWS.)

chunks.title: Amazon ECS: EC2 vs Fargate launch types
chunks.text:
Scenario: A laboratory runs a steady containerized analysis service on Amazon ECS. The infrastructure team has an approved process for managing container hosts and requires capacity reservations for a specific EC2 instance type. Which option meets the team's requirements?
Correct: Run the service on EC2 instances managed by the infrastructure team.
Why: This team needs capacity reservations for a specific EC2 instance type and intends to manage its hosts. Those are documented reasons to choose ECS on EC2. Fargate is designed to avoid server management, so it does not meet the required instance control. ECS Managed Instances shifts underlying infrastructure management to AWS.
Wrong options: Run the service on ECS Managed Instances and delegate host maintenance to AWS. (Delegating host maintenance conflicts with the team's stated host-management process.); Run the service on servers registered through ECS Anywhere. (External servers do not fulfill the requirement for capacity reservations of an EC2 instance type.); Run the service on Fargate and let ECS select the host capacity. (Fargate avoids host management rather than letting the team manage a reserved, specific instance type.)

chunks.title: Amazon EKS (managed Kubernetes)
chunks.text:
Amazon EKS (managed Kubernetes). Amazon EKS runs Kubernetes clusters on AWS and supports Kubernetes-compatible applications and community tooling. Choose it when Kubernetes compatibility is a requirement; use EKS Auto Mode when the team also wants EKS to manage nodes.
When to use: A team must keep using Kubernetes-compatible applications, tooling, or plugins without refactoring.; A team needs a managed Kubernetes control plane on AWS.; A Kubernetes team wants automated node provisioning, scaling, and operating system patching.
Key facts: EKS is certified Kubernetes-conformant.; EKS standard manages the Kubernetes control plane.; EKS Auto Mode also manages nodes, including infrastructure provisioning, scaling, and operating system patching.; EKS Capabilities include managed Argo CD for GitOps-based continuous deployment.; EKS has per-cluster pricing; resources used to run applications are charged separately.
Gotchas: Managed control plane does not mean EKS standard provides every node-management feature of EKS Auto Mode.; Do not choose a different container orchestrator when retaining Kubernetes tooling is an explicit requirement.; Do not assume the EKS cluster charge includes the compute used by application workloads.
Confused with: Amazon ECS: EKS is the choice when Kubernetes compatibility or existing Kubernetes tooling is required.; AWS Fargate: Fargate addresses running containers without managing servers; EKS addresses the Kubernetes requirement.; AWS Batch: Batch addresses queued batch jobs, not a requirement to retain Kubernetes orchestration.
ES: Amazon EKS ejecuta clústeres de Kubernetes en AWS y admite aplicaciones y herramientas compatibles con Kubernetes. Elígelo cuando la compatibilidad con Kubernetes sea un requisito; usa EKS Auto Mode si el equipo también quiere que EKS administre los nodos. EKS cuenta con certificación de conformidad con Kubernetes.; EKS standard administra el plano de control de Kubernetes.; EKS Auto Mode también administra los nodos, incluido el aprovisionamiento de infraestructura, el escalado y la aplicación de parches del sistema operativo.; EKS Capabilities incluye Argo CD administrado para el despliegue continuo basado en GitOps.; EKS tiene un cargo por clúster; los recursos utilizados para ejecutar las aplicaciones se cobran por separado.

chunks.title: Amazon EKS (managed Kubernetes)
chunks.text:
Scenario: A video production company is moving several containerized services to AWS. Its platform team already deploys the services with Kubernetes-compatible configurations and uses Kubernetes community plugins. The team must keep those deployment practices without refactoring the applications. Which solution meets these requirements with the LEAST migration effort?
Correct: Deploy the services to an Amazon EKS cluster.
Why: The deciding requirement is to keep Kubernetes deployment practices without refactoring. Amazon EKS is Kubernetes-conformant and supports Kubernetes-compatible applications and community tooling. Amazon ECS is a plausible container orchestrator, but it does not meet the explicit Kubernetes-tooling requirement.
Wrong options: Deploy the containers as Amazon ECS services on EC2 instances. (ECS provides container orchestration but does not satisfy the stated need to retain Kubernetes tooling.); Deploy the application with AWS Elastic Beanstalk. (A managed application platform does not meet the requirement to continue using Kubernetes plugins and configurations.); Deploy the services as AWS Lambda functions. (Moving the existing containerized services to functions does not preserve their Kubernetes deployment practices.)

chunks.title: Amazon EKS (managed Kubernetes)
chunks.text:
Scenario: A publishing company operates Kubernetes clusters for its editorial services on AWS. Its deployment team wants GitOps-based continuous deployment with Argo CD, but does not want to install and maintain that platform component in each cluster. Which solution meets these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?
Correct: Use managed Argo CD through Amazon EKS Capabilities.
Why: The company specifically needs Argo CD-based deployment for its Kubernetes clusters while avoiding component maintenance. EKS Capabilities provides managed Argo CD and reduces the burden of installing, maintaining, and scaling that component. Installing Argo CD in every cluster preserves the tool but fails the operational-overhead requirement.
Wrong options: Move the services to Amazon ECS and continue using the Kubernetes deployments. (Changing orchestrators does not satisfy the requirement to keep Kubernetes clusters and deployment practices.); Use EKS standard and install and maintain Argo CD in each cluster. (This retains Argo CD but leaves the installation and maintenance work the team wants to avoid.); Use AWS Controllers for Kubernetes (ACK) through EKS Capabilities for deployments. (ACK manages AWS resources through Kubernetes but is not the managed Argo CD capability requested for GitOps deployment.)

chunks.title: Amazon MQ (ActiveMQ/RabbitMQ)
chunks.text:
Amazon MQ (ActiveMQ/RabbitMQ). Amazon MQ is a managed broker service for Apache ActiveMQ Classic and RabbitMQ. Choose it when an application must keep its existing broker-based messaging code while AWS handles broker setup, operation, and maintenance.
When to use: An existing ActiveMQ Classic or RabbitMQ application is moving to AWS without rewriting messaging code.; Applications must continue communicating through a message broker that uses established messaging protocols.
Key facts: Amazon MQ supports managed Apache ActiveMQ Classic and RabbitMQ brokers.; Existing message brokers can be migrated to Amazon MQ without rewriting messaging code.; Amazon MQ performs broker maintenance and version upgrades during a scheduled maintenance window.; Broker and queue metrics are automatically collected and pushed to Amazon CloudWatch every minute.; Amazon MQ encrypts messages at rest and in transit; broker connections use SSL and can be restricted to a private endpoint in an Amazon VPC.
Gotchas: A managed queue is not necessarily a replacement for an application that must retain its existing broker messaging code.; Choosing a service for fan-out or event routing does not, by itself, meet a broker-compatibility requirement.
Confused with: Amazon SQS: Choose Amazon MQ when preserving existing broker messaging code is required; SQS is a managed queue, not a migrated ActiveMQ Classic or RabbitMQ broker.; Amazon SNS: SNS distributes notifications to subscribers; Amazon MQ provides a managed broker for existing broker-based applications.; Amazon EventBridge: EventBridge routes events with rules; Amazon MQ addresses a requirement to retain broker-based messaging code.
ES: Amazon MQ es un servicio de brokers administrados para Apache ActiveMQ Classic y RabbitMQ. Elígelo cuando una aplicación deba conservar su código de mensajería existente mientras AWS se encarga de la configuración, operación y mantenimiento del broker. Amazon MQ ofrece brokers administrados de Apache ActiveMQ Classic y RabbitMQ.; Puedes migrar brokers existentes a Amazon MQ sin reescribir el código de mensajería.; Amazon MQ realiza el mantenimiento y las actualizaciones de versión del broker durante una ventana de mantenimiento programada.; Las métricas del broker y de las colas se recopilan y envían automáticamente a Amazon CloudWatch cada minuto.; Amazon MQ cifra los mensajes en reposo y en tránsito; las conexiones al broker usan SSL y pueden restringirse a un endpoint privado en una Amazon VPC.

chunks.title: Amazon MQ (ActiveMQ/RabbitMQ)
chunks.text:
Scenario: A publishing company runs an order-processing application with an Apache ActiveMQ Classic broker in its data center. The company is moving the application to AWS and will not change its messaging code during the migration. Which solution meets these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?
Correct: Migrate the ActiveMQ Classic broker to Amazon MQ.
Why: The deciding constraints are the existing ActiveMQ Classic broker and the prohibition on changing messaging code. Amazon MQ supports migration of existing brokers without rewriting that code and manages broker setup, operation, and maintenance. Running ActiveMQ Classic on EC2 could preserve the application behavior but leaves broker maintenance with the company. SQS and SNS would require a messaging redesign.
Wrong options: Run an ActiveMQ Classic broker on Amazon EC2 and maintain it internally. (This could retain the broker, but the company would still operate and maintain it.); Move messaging to Amazon SQS and update the application to use queues. (SQS would require changing the application's existing broker messaging code.); Publish order events to Amazon SNS and subscribe the processing application. (Moving to SNS would replace the existing broker messaging approach and require application changes.)

chunks.title: Amazon MQ (ActiveMQ/RabbitMQ)
chunks.text:
Scenario: A healthcare software provider is moving a RabbitMQ-based application to AWS. Its integration team must retain the application's broker messaging code, and the security team requires encrypted broker connections and access through a private endpoint in an Amazon VPC. Which solution meets these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?
Correct: Use a RabbitMQ broker on Amazon MQ with SSL connections and a private endpoint.
Why: The application must keep its RabbitMQ messaging code while using encrypted, private broker connectivity. Amazon MQ manages RabbitMQ brokers, uses SSL for broker connections, and can restrict access to a private endpoint within a VPC. A self-managed EC2 broker could satisfy the connectivity needs but adds operational work. EventBridge and SQS do not satisfy the code-retention requirement.
Wrong options: Replace RabbitMQ with Amazon EventBridge rules and restrict event publishers to the VPC. (EventBridge rules do not preserve the application's RabbitMQ broker messaging code.); Replace RabbitMQ with Amazon SQS queues and place consumers in private subnets. (Using SQS would require changing the existing broker messaging code.); Install RabbitMQ on Amazon EC2 instances in private subnets and enable SSL. (This can address connectivity requirements but leaves broker operation and maintenance to the provider.)

chunks.title: Amazon MSK (managed Apache Kafka)
chunks.text:
Amazon MSK (managed Apache Kafka). Amazon MSK runs Apache Kafka workloads as a managed service while retaining Kafka producer and consumer operations. Choose it when existing Kafka applications and tooling must keep working; choose MSK Serverless when managing and scaling cluster capacity is also undesirable.
When to use: Existing Apache Kafka producers, consumers, tooling, or plugins must continue working without application-code changes.; A Kafka workload needs managed clusters but requires control over broker count or type: consider MSK Provisioned.; A Kafka workload should avoid managing and scaling cluster capacity: consider MSK Serverless.
Key facts: MSK runs open-source Apache Kafka and supports existing Kafka applications, tooling, and plugins without application-code changes.; MSK handles cluster control-plane operations; applications use Kafka data-plane operations to create topics and produce and consume data.; MSK Provisioned lets you specify broker nodes per Availability Zone and update broker number and type.; MSK Serverless manages broker nodes and removes the need to manage and scale cluster capacity.; MSK Connect streams data to and from a Kafka cluster; MSK Replicator replicates data across MSK Provisioned clusters in the same or different AWS Regions.
Gotchas: A managed streaming service is not necessarily Kafka-compatible: do not substitute Kinesis Data Streams when unchanged Kafka applications are required.; Data Firehose targets buffered delivery to destinations; that is a different requirement from retaining Kafka producers and consumers.; MSK Serverless is not the choice when the team must specify and update broker number and type.
Confused with: kinesis-data-streams: Use Kinesis Data Streams for its stream-consumer and replay pattern; use MSK when existing Kafka applications must remain compatible.; data-firehose: Use Data Firehose for buffered delivery to destinations such as S3; use MSK to run Kafka producer and consumer workloads.
ES: Amazon MSK ejecuta cargas de Apache Kafka como servicio administrado y conserva las operaciones de productores y consumidores de Kafka. Elígelo cuando las aplicaciones y herramientas existentes de Kafka deban seguir funcionando; elige MSK Serverless si también necesitas evitar la administración y el escalamiento de la capacidad del clúster. MSK ejecuta versiones de código abierto de Apache Kafka y admite aplicaciones, herramientas y plugins existentes sin cambios en el código de las aplicaciones.; MSK se encarga de las operaciones del plano de control del clúster; las aplicaciones usan operaciones del plano de datos de Kafka para crear temas, producir y consumir datos.; MSK Provisioned te permite especificar brokers por Availability Zone y actualizar su cantidad y tipo.; MSK Serverless administra los brokers y elimina la necesidad de administrar y escalar la capacidad del clúster.; MSK Connect transmite datos hacia y desde un clúster de Kafka; MSK Replicator replica datos entre clústeres de MSK Provisioned en la misma AWS Region o en distintas.

chunks.title: Amazon MSK (managed Apache Kafka)
chunks.text:
Scenario: A ticketing company is moving a live event pipeline to AWS. Its applications already produce to and consume from Apache Kafka topics, and the team cannot change their application code. Traffic varies sharply between events, and the team does not want to manage or scale cluster capacity. Which solution meets these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?
Correct: Use Amazon MSK Serverless for the existing Kafka applications.
Why: The deciding requirements are unchanged Kafka applications and no cluster-capacity management. MSK runs Apache Kafka workloads without requiring application-code changes, and MSK Serverless manages the broker nodes and cluster capacity. MSK Provisioned also fits the compatibility requirement, but choosing and adjusting brokers conflicts with the requested operational model. Kinesis Data Streams and Data Firehose address different ingestion patterns rather than preserving the existing Kafka workload.
Wrong options: Move the producers and consumers to Kinesis Data Streams with on-demand capacity. (On-demand capacity does not meet the requirement to keep the existing Kafka applications unchanged.); Send the events through Amazon Data Firehose to an S3 bucket. (Buffered delivery to S3 does not preserve the required Kafka producer-and-consumer workload.); Use Amazon MSK Provisioned and adjust the broker configuration for each event. (MSK Provisioned retains Kafka compatibility but leaves the team responsible for broker-capacity choices.)

chunks.title: Amazon MSK (managed Apache Kafka)
chunks.text:
Scenario: A media company operates two MSK Provisioned clusters in different AWS Regions. Its Kafka applications will continue to use both clusters, and the company wants to replicate streaming data between them rather than deliver it to an analytics destination. Which solution meets these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?
Correct: Use MSK Replicator between the two MSK Provisioned clusters.
Why: The requirement is replication between MSK Provisioned clusters in different AWS Regions. MSK Replicator is the documented feature for reliably replicating data across such clusters. MSK Connect serves the broader task of streaming data to and from Kafka, but it is not the specifically identified cross-cluster replication feature. Sending data to S3 or replacing a Kafka cluster with another stream misses the stated destination.
Wrong options: Use MSK Connect to stream data to and from one cluster. (MSK Connect supports streaming data to and from a Kafka cluster, but MSK Replicator directly addresses replication between these clusters.); Use Kinesis Data Streams as a replacement stream in the second Region. (A replacement stream does not replicate data between the existing Kafka clusters.); Use Amazon Data Firehose to deliver the data to S3 in the second Region. (Delivery to S3 does not meet the requirement to replicate data between the two MSK Provisioned clusters.)

chunks.title: API Gateway authorization: IAM, Cognito, Lambda authorizers, private APIs
chunks.text:
API Gateway authorization: IAM, Cognito, Lambda authorizers, private APIs. Choose API Gateway REST API authorization based on who calls the API and what evidence of access they provide. Use Cognito user pool authorizers for user-pool identities, IAM for AWS identities, Lambda authorizers for custom tokens or request attributes, and private REST APIs with resource policies for VPC-restricted access.
When to use: Callers already authenticate with an Amazon Cognito user pool.; AWS roles or users need permission to invoke an API or individual methods.; Access decisions depend on a bearer token or request headers, paths, or query strings.; A REST API must be reachable only through private VPC connectivity.
Key facts: IAM policies can control who invokes an entire REST API or individual methods.; Lambda authorizers can use bearer tokens and request parameters to control method invocation.; A private API is a REST API callable only from within an Amazon VPC through an interface VPC endpoint.; A resource policy can restrict private API access with aws:SourceVpc or aws:SourceVpce conditions.; VPC endpoint policies provide additional control over access through interface VPC endpoints.
Gotchas: An API key and usage plan track and limit customer usage; they are not a substitute for choosing an authorization mechanism.; A source IP resource policy does not turn a public API into a private API.; A private API endpoint supports REST APIs, not other API Gateway API types.
Confused with: 
ES: Elige la autorización de una REST API de API Gateway según quién llama y qué información presenta para obtener acceso. Usa Amazon Cognito user pool authorizers para identidades del user pool, IAM para identidades de AWS, Lambda authorizers para tokens o atributos personalizados, y private REST APIs con resource policies para restringir el acceso desde una VPC. Las IAM policies pueden controlar quién invoca una REST API completa o métodos individuales.; Los Lambda authorizers pueden usar bearer tokens y parámetros de la solicitud para controlar la invocación de métodos.; Una private API es una REST API invocable solo desde una Amazon VPC mediante un interface VPC endpoint.; Una resource policy puede restringir el acceso a una private API con condiciones aws:SourceVpc o aws:SourceVpce.; Las VPC endpoint policies agregan control sobre el acceso que pasa por interface VPC endpoints.

chunks.title: API Gateway authorization: IAM, Cognito, Lambda authorizers, private APIs
chunks.text:
Scenario: A media company has several internal applications whose AWS roles call a REST API. Each application should be allowed to invoke only the methods it needs, and the company wants to manage those permissions through its existing AWS identity controls. Which solution meets these requirements?
Correct: Use IAM roles and policies to control invocation of individual API methods.
Why: The callers are AWS roles, and permissions must vary by method. IAM roles and policies provide invocation controls for an entire REST API or individual methods, matching both constraints. A source IP policy would not distinguish the applications' role-based permissions, even if their requests came from a known range.
Wrong options: Use a resource policy that allows the applications' shared source IP range. (A shared source IP range does not distinguish the roles' different method-level permissions.); Use a Cognito user pool authorizer for the applications' API calls. (A user pool authorizer does not meet the requirement to manage permissions through the applications' existing AWS roles.); Use a Lambda authorizer that maintains separate method rules for each application. (Custom Lambda rules duplicate the existing AWS identity controls the company wants to use.)

chunks.title: API Gateway authorization: IAM, Cognito, Lambda authorizers, private APIs
chunks.text:
Scenario: A research organization is deploying a REST API for workloads in an Amazon VPC. The API must be callable without traversing the public internet, and its access policy must reject calls that do not originate from one designated VPC endpoint. Which two actions meet these requirements? (Choose two.)
Correct: Add an aws:SourceVpce condition for the designated endpoint to the API resource policy. + Deploy the API as a private REST API accessed through an interface VPC endpoint.
Why: The organization needs both private network access and an API-side restriction to one endpoint. A private REST API reached through an interface VPC endpoint meets the connectivity requirement; an aws:SourceVpce condition in its resource policy limits the allowed endpoint. A VPC endpoint policy can add control over traffic through an endpoint, but permitting traffic there does not replace the requested restriction in the API's access policy.
Wrong options: Attach a VPC endpoint policy that permits requests to the API. (An endpoint policy controls access through that endpoint but does not make the API's resource policy reject other sources.); Deploy a Regional REST API and use AWS WAF to filter incoming requests. (AWS WAF addresses common web exploits, not the requirement for a private API endpoint.); Require an API key through a usage plan for each VPC workload. (Usage plans track and limit API use but do not provide private connectivity or restrict requests to a VPC endpoint.)

chunks.title: Amazon API Gateway: REST vs HTTP vs WebSocket APIs
chunks.text:
Amazon API Gateway: REST vs HTTP vs WebSocket APIs. Amazon API Gateway provides managed REST, HTTP, and WebSocket APIs in front of Lambda functions, AWS services, and web backends. Choose an HTTP API for a lower-priced RESTful API when its features suffice, a REST API for capabilities such as caching or private endpoints, and a WebSocket API for stateful, full-duplex communication.
When to use: Choose an HTTP API for a RESTful endpoint that needs Lambda or HTTP integration but no REST-only features.; Choose a REST API when requirements include API keys, per-client throttling, request validation, caching, AWS WAF integration, or a private API endpoint.; Choose a WebSocket API when clients and the server must exchange messages over a stateful, full-duplex connection.
Key facts: REST APIs and HTTP APIs both support Lambda functions, AWS services, and public HTTP endpoints as integrations.; HTTP APIs are offered at a lower price than REST APIs and support JWT authorization.; Private API endpoints, API keys, caching, and request validation are available for REST APIs but not HTTP APIs.; Both REST APIs and HTTP APIs support regional endpoints; only REST APIs support edge-optimized and private endpoint types.; WebSocket APIs can route incoming messages based on message content.
Gotchas: Do not choose an HTTP API solely because it supports Lambda if the scenario also requires API Gateway caching or API keys.; A private integration to a load balancer is not the same requirement as a private API endpoint; HTTP APIs support the former, not the latter.; Do not choose a REST or HTTP API when the requirement is a stateful, full-duplex client-server connection.
Confused with: HTTP API vs REST API: Both can expose RESTful backends, but REST APIs provide features such as private endpoints and caching; HTTP APIs have a lower price when those features are unnecessary.; WebSocket API vs RESTful API: WebSocket APIs support stateful, full-duplex messaging; REST and HTTP APIs use stateless client-server communication.
ES: Amazon API Gateway ofrece API REST, HTTP y WebSocket administradas delante de funciones Lambda, servicios de AWS y aplicaciones web. Elige una HTTP API para una API RESTful de menor precio si sus funciones bastan, una REST API si necesitas capacidades como caching o private API endpoints, y una WebSocket API para comunicación stateful y full-duplex. Tanto REST APIs como HTTP APIs admiten integraciones con funciones Lambda, servicios de AWS y endpoints HTTP públicos.; HTTP APIs tienen un precio menor que REST APIs y admiten autorización JWT.; Private API endpoints, API keys, caching y request validation están disponibles en REST APIs, pero no en HTTP APIs.; REST APIs y HTTP APIs admiten endpoints regionales; solo REST APIs admiten los tipos edge-optimized y private.; WebSocket APIs pueden enrutar mensajes entrantes según su contenido.

chunks.title: Amazon API Gateway: REST vs HTTP vs WebSocket APIs
chunks.text:
Scenario: A logistics company is building a dispatcher console. While an operator is connected, the backend must send new vehicle assignments to the console, and the operator must send acknowledgments over the same connection. Incoming messages must be routed according to their content. Which API Gateway API type best meets these requirements?
Correct: A WebSocket API that routes messages based on their content
Why: The console needs the client and server to exchange messages over the same connection. WebSocket APIs support stateful, full-duplex communication and can route incoming messages based on content. REST and HTTP APIs are stateless, even when they integrate with Lambda. Adding REST API caching does not change that communication model.
Wrong options: A REST API with caching enabled for assignment responses (Caching responses does not provide stateful, full-duplex messaging.); A REST API that invokes a Lambda function for each client request (A REST API uses stateless communication and does not meet the same-connection, full-duplex requirement.); An HTTP API that invokes a Lambda function for each client request (An HTTP API uses stateless communication rather than the required full-duplex connection.)

chunks.title: Amazon API Gateway: REST vs HTTP vs WebSocket APIs
chunks.text:
Scenario: A public museum exposes a regional API backed by an HTTP application. Most visitors repeatedly request the same exhibit descriptions, and the museum wants responses cached at API Gateway. It also requires request validation before requests reach the application. Which solution meets both requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?
Correct: A REST API with caching and request validation enabled
Why: Both caching at API Gateway and request validation are explicit requirements. REST APIs support both features, as well as regional endpoints and HTTP backend integrations. HTTP APIs can use an HTTP backend but do not provide either required gateway feature. Moving those tasks into the application also fails the specified caching location and adds operational work.
Wrong options: A WebSocket API with the application caching exhibit messages (A WebSocket API does not provide the requested RESTful response caching and request validation at API Gateway.); An HTTP API with a regional endpoint and HTTP backend integration (An HTTP API supports the backend integration but not API Gateway caching or request validation.); An HTTP API with the application implementing caching and request validation (Application-level caching is not the required caching at API Gateway and adds application work.)

chunks.title: Amazon API Gateway: REST vs HTTP vs WebSocket APIs
chunks.text:
Scenario: A ticketing startup is exposing Lambda functions to a mobile app through standard HTTP methods. The app will send JWTs, and the team does not need API keys, caching, or private API endpoints. Which API Gateway API type meets these requirements MOST cost-effectively?
Correct: An HTTP API with a Lambda integration and JWT authorization
Why: The deciding requirement is a lower-priced RESTful API that accepts JWTs and invokes Lambda. HTTP APIs support both JWT authorization and Lambda integrations and are offered at a lower price than REST APIs. A REST API would work as a backend front door, but its additional capabilities do not satisfy any stated need. A WebSocket API addresses a different communication pattern.
Wrong options: A REST API with API keys for each mobile user (The scenario does not require API keys, so this adds a REST-only capability without meeting the cost priority.); A REST API with a Lambda integration (A REST API can integrate with Lambda, but its additional features are unnecessary for this lower-priced API requirement.); A WebSocket API with a Lambda backend (A WebSocket API is intended for stateful, full-duplex communication rather than the stated RESTful requests.)

chunks.title: API Gateway throttling, usage plans and caching
chunks.text:
API Gateway throttling, usage plans and caching. API Gateway REST API throttling sets rate and burst targets to protect integrations from excess requests; usage plans add per-client targets through API keys. Stage caching can reduce integration calls and latency when responses can be reused.
When to use: Different clients need different request-rate or quota targets.; A stage or method needs protection from traffic spikes.; Repeated GET requests can reuse responses instead of calling the integration.
Key facts: Throttles and quotas are best-effort targets, not guaranteed ceilings.; Rate is the rate at which tokens are added to the token bucket; burst is its capacity. Throttled clients may receive HTTP 429 responses.; Usage plans identify clients by associated API keys for per-client throttling.; Stage caching applies to GET methods by default. The default TTL is 300 seconds; the maximum is 3600 seconds.; Cache capacity is billed by the hour. CacheHitCount and CacheMissCount show cache activity.
Gotchas: A stage-level throttle alone does not provide different targets for individual clients.; Enabling stage caching does not automatically cache non-GET methods.; A cache key that omits a response-changing parameter can reuse the wrong response.; A method-level cache setting is not active until a cache cluster is provisioned for the stage.
Confused with: 
ES: El throttling de una REST API en API Gateway establece objetivos de rate y burst para proteger la integración del exceso de solicitudes; los usage plans agregan objetivos por cliente mediante API keys. El caché de una stage puede reducir las llamadas a la integración y la latencia cuando las respuestas se pueden reutilizar. Los límites de throttling y las cuotas son objetivos best-effort, no topes garantizados.; Rate indica la velocidad a la que se agregan tokens al token bucket; burst es su capacidad. Los clientes limitados pueden recibir respuestas HTTP 429.; Los usage plans identifican a los clientes mediante API keys asociadas para aplicar throttling por cliente.; El caché de una stage se aplica por defecto a métodos GET. El TTL predeterminado es de 300 segundos y el máximo es de 3600 segundos.; La capacidad del caché se cobra por hora. CacheHitCount y CacheMissCount muestran su actividad.

chunks.title: API Gateway throttling, usage plans and caching
chunks.text:
Scenario: A public library's REST API serves the same GET /catalog response to many readers, while a few catalog partners also submit heavy bursts across other methods. The library wants fewer integration calls for repeated GET requests and distinct request-rate targets for each partner, without changing its integration. Which TWO API Gateway configurations meet these requirements? (Choose two.)
Correct: Create usage plans with rate targets and associate each partner's API key with its plan. + Provision a stage cache and enable caching for GET /catalog.
Why: The library has two separate requirements: reuse repeated GET responses and set different rate targets for partners. Provisioning a stage cache and enabling GET /catalog caching addresses the first; usage plans associated with partner API keys address the second. A method cache without a provisioned stage cache cluster is not active. Shared stage or method throttling targets cannot differentiate the partners.
Wrong options: Set a common method-level burst target on the other methods for all partners. (A shared method target may address bursts but does not assign distinct rate targets to individual partners.); Enable GET /catalog method caching without provisioning a stage cache cluster. (Method caching is inactive until a cache cluster is provisioned for the stage.); Set one stage-level throttle target and use it as the distinct target for every partner. (A single stage target does not provide distinct per-partner rate targets.)

chunks.title: API Gateway throttling, usage plans and caching
chunks.text:
Scenario: A research institute has a REST API stage with a costly POST /simulations method and several lightweight GET methods. Traffic bursts to POST /simulations threaten the integration, but the GET methods should keep their existing request capacity. Which configuration meets these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?
Correct: Set a lower throttling rate and burst target for POST /simulations at the method level.
Why: Only POST /simulations needs a lower traffic target. API Gateway supports per-method throttling targets for a stage, so the institute can limit that method without imposing the same target on its GET methods. Lowering a target across the stage would affect the lightweight methods too. Default stage caching applies to GET, not POST, and does not establish a throttling target.
Wrong options: Lower the stage-level throttling targets equally for every method. (The shared target would also constrain the GET methods that should retain their request capacity.); Assign an API key and the same usage-plan target to every caller of the stage. (A shared per-client target does not isolate the POST method while preserving GET capacity.); Enable the stage cache and rely on its default settings to cache POST /simulations. (Stage caching enables GET caching by default, not POST caching, and caching does not set a burst target.)

chunks.title: Amazon AppFlow (SaaS data integration)
chunks.text:
Amazon AppFlow (SaaS data integration). Amazon AppFlow is a fully managed service for moving data between SaaS applications and AWS services without writing integration code. Choose it when a scenario calls for a managed flow from a supported SaaS source to Amazon S3 or Amazon Redshift.
When to use: Move Salesforce records to Amazon Redshift or Zendesk tickets to Amazon S3 without writing integration code.; Run SaaS data transfers on demand or on a schedule.; Transfer supported SaaS data privately over AWS infrastructure by using AppFlow with AWS PrivateLink.
Key facts: AppFlow flows can run on demand or on a schedule.; AppFlow encrypts transferred data at rest and in transit.; AppFlow integrates with AWS PrivateLink for private data transfer.; Data transferred to Amazon S3 can be cataloged in the AWS Glue Data Catalog.; AppFlow can ingest Salesforce Platform events and Change Data Capture events for publication to an Amazon EventBridge partner event bus.
Gotchas: AWS Glue Data Catalog helps users discover data; it is not the SaaS-to-S3 flow in this scenario.; AWS CloudTrail records AppFlow API activity, not the Salesforce or Zendesk records being transferred.; AWS CloudFormation can provision AppFlow resources, but provisioning alone does not move SaaS data.
Confused with: AWS Glue Data Catalog: Catalogs data for discovery; AppFlow performs the SaaS-to-AWS transfer.; Amazon EventBridge: Routes matching events; AppFlow can ingest supported Salesforce events and publish them to an EventBridge partner event bus.
ES: Amazon AppFlow es un servicio totalmente administrado que mueve datos entre aplicaciones SaaS y servicios de AWS sin que tengas que escribir código de integración. Elígelo cuando necesites un flujo administrado desde una fuente SaaS compatible hacia Amazon S3 o Amazon Redshift. Los flujos de AppFlow pueden ejecutarse bajo demanda o según una programación.; AppFlow cifra los datos transferidos en reposo y en tránsito.; AppFlow se integra con AWS PrivateLink para transferencias privadas.; Puedes catalogar en AWS Glue Data Catalog los datos transferidos a Amazon S3.; AppFlow puede ingerir eventos de Salesforce Platform y Change Data Capture para publicarlos en un bus de eventos de socios de Amazon EventBridge.

chunks.title: Amazon AppFlow (SaaS data integration)
chunks.text:
Scenario: A healthcare support team needs to copy Zendesk tickets to Amazon S3 for analysis when an analyst requests a transfer. Its security policy requires the transfer to use AWS infrastructure instead of the public internet, and the team wants no custom connector code. Which solution meets these requirements MOST securely?
Correct: Run an on-demand Amazon AppFlow flow from Zendesk to Amazon S3 with private data transfer through AWS PrivateLink.
Why: The deciding constraints are an on-demand Zendesk-to-S3 transfer and a path over AWS infrastructure rather than the public internet. Amazon AppFlow supports on-demand flows, and its AWS PrivateLink integration provides private data transfer. An AppFlow flow without that option meets the transfer requirement but misses the security requirement. Cataloging or logging does not move the tickets.
Wrong options: Use AWS CloudTrail to record AppFlow API calls and deliver those logs to Amazon S3. (API logs are not the requested Zendesk tickets.); Create an AWS Glue Data Catalog entry for the Zendesk tickets in Amazon S3. (A catalog entry helps users discover data but does not copy tickets from Zendesk.); Run an on-demand Amazon AppFlow flow from Zendesk to Amazon S3 without enabling private data transfer. (The flow addresses the source and destination but omits the required private data transfer option.)

chunks.title: Amazon AppFlow (SaaS data integration)
chunks.text:
Scenario: A subscription company receives Salesforce Change Data Capture events and wants matching events routed to AWS Lambda for downstream processing. The company prefers a managed way to ingest the Salesforce events into an Amazon EventBridge partner event bus rather than building its own Salesforce ingestion code. Which solution meets these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?
Correct: Use Amazon AppFlow to ingest the Salesforce events into an EventBridge partner event bus, then configure an EventBridge rule that targets Lambda.
Why: The requirement is to ingest Salesforce Change Data Capture events into an EventBridge partner event bus without building Salesforce ingestion code. Amazon AppFlow supports that ingestion, and EventBridge rules can route matching events to Lambda. A scheduled flow to S3 is a valid data-transfer pattern, but it misses the required event-bus destination. CloudTrail records AppFlow API calls, not the Salesforce events requested here.
Wrong options: Write a Lambda function that ingests Salesforce events and publishes them to an EventBridge partner event bus. (Custom Salesforce ingestion code violates the company's stated preference.); Record Amazon AppFlow API activity with AWS CloudTrail and create an EventBridge rule for the CloudTrail records. (AppFlow API activity is not the Salesforce Change Data Capture event stream the company needs.); Create a scheduled Amazon AppFlow flow that transfers Salesforce records to Amazon S3, then catalog the files. (A scheduled S3 data flow does not deliver the requested events to an EventBridge partner event bus.)

chunks.title: AWS Application Migration Service (MGN) lift-and-shift
chunks.text:
AWS Application Migration Service (MGN) lift-and-shift. AWS Application Migration Service (MGN) rehosts physical, virtual, and cloud servers on AWS through continuous block-level replication and a migration cutover with minimal downtime. Choose it when the goal is to move whole servers rather than migrate only a database or maintain a disaster-recovery standby.
When to use: Move physical, VMware, Hyper-V, or cloud servers to AWS without first refactoring their applications.; Keep source servers running during replication and minimize downtime at cutover.; Coordinate a large migration in application groups and waves.
Key facts: MGN continuously replicates source servers at the block level and converts them for launch on AWS.; Cutover windows are typically measured in minutes.; Replication, launch, and post-launch templates set defaults for newly added servers; individual servers can have overrides.; Servers can be grouped into applications and applications into waves for bulk actions, including launch and cutover.; MGN can replicate into standard Availability Zones or AWS Local Zones without special configuration.
Gotchas: Continuous replication alone does not identify the right service: the objective must be migration and cutover, not ongoing disaster recovery.; DMS moves database data; it does not rehost an entire application server.; MGN is a rehosting first step, not a requirement to refactor the application before migration.
Confused with: AWS DMS and Schema Conversion: Choose DMS for database migration; add schema conversion when changing to a heterogeneous database engine.; AWS Elastic Disaster Recovery: Choose Elastic Disaster Recovery to keep servers ready for recovery; choose MGN to migrate them and complete a cutover.
ES: AWS Application Migration Service (MGN) permite rehost de servidores físicos, virtuales y en la nube en AWS mediante replicación continua a nivel de bloques y un cutover de migración con tiempo de inactividad mínimo. Elígelo cuando necesitas trasladar servidores completos, no solo migrar una base de datos o mantener un entorno de disaster recovery. MGN replica continuamente los servidores de origen a nivel de bloques y los convierte para iniciarlos en AWS.; Las ventanas de cutover suelen medirse en minutos.; Las plantillas de replicación, launch y post-launch definen valores iniciales para servidores nuevos; puedes configurar excepciones por servidor.; Puedes agrupar servidores en aplicaciones y aplicaciones en waves para ejecutar acciones masivas, como launch y cutover.; MGN puede replicar en Availability Zones estándar o AWS Local Zones sin configuración especial.

chunks.title: AWS Application Migration Service (MGN) lift-and-shift
chunks.text:
Scenario: A manufacturer plans to move several groups of legacy production servers to AWS without refactoring them. Source servers must remain in service while changes are replicated, and each group must have a scheduled migration cutover rather than remain a permanent disaster-recovery environment. Which two actions best meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead? (Choose two.)
Correct: Use AWS Application Migration Service for continuous block-level replication of the source servers. + Organize the MGN servers into applications and waves to coordinate group cutovers.
Why: The manufacturer needs both continuous replication of entire servers and coordinated migration cutovers. MGN supplies block-level server replication, and its applications and waves support bulk cutover actions. DMS addresses database migration rather than whole servers. An ongoing Elastic Disaster Recovery environment serves a recovery objective, not the requested completed migration.
Wrong options: Use AWS Elastic Disaster Recovery to keep each server group as a continuing recovery environment. (A continuing recovery environment does not satisfy the requirement to complete scheduled migrations.); Use AWS DMS full load and change data capture as the migration process for every application server. (DMS can migrate databases but does not rehost the complete legacy servers.); Rebuild each server on EC2 and transfer its data only during that group's cutover. (Rebuilding adds work and transferring data only at cutover misses the continuous-replication requirement.)

chunks.title: AWS Application Migration Service (MGN) lift-and-shift
chunks.text:
Scenario: A regional wholesaler runs its ordering application on physical servers and VMware virtual machines. The company wants to move the servers to AWS without changing the application, while keeping the source systems running until a short migration cutover. Which solution meets these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?
Correct: Use AWS Application Migration Service to replicate the servers continuously and launch the migrated servers on AWS at cutover.
Why: The deciding requirement is to rehost entire physical and virtual servers without changing the application. MGN continuously replicates source servers and converts them for launch on AWS, supporting a short cutover. DMS is aimed at database migration, not the complete servers. Rebuilding the application also adds operational work that the scenario seeks to avoid.
Wrong options: Use AWS Elastic Disaster Recovery to maintain a recovery environment instead of planning a migration cutover. (A continuing disaster-recovery arrangement does not address the stated goal of completing a server migration.); Use AWS DMS to replicate the application's database, then rebuild the application servers separately. (DMS addresses database migration but leaves the required whole-server rehosting to a separate process.); Rebuild the application on new EC2 instances and transfer its data during the cutover window. (Rebuilding the servers adds work when the requirement is to rehost the existing application with minimal cutover downtime.)

chunks.title: ASG health checks, warm pools and lifecycle hooks
chunks.text:
ASG health checks, warm pools and lifecycle hooks. An Auto Scaling group replaces instances it determines are unhealthy, but Elastic Load Balancing health checks must be enabled for the group if load balancer health should trigger replacement. Use lifecycle hooks to pause launch or termination for required work; with a warm pool, a launch hook can keep an instance from being stopped or hibernated before bootstrap finishes.
When to use: Instances fail load balancer health checks and must be replaced automatically.; New instances must finish bootstrap before receiving traffic.; Logs or other data must be collected before scale-in termination.; Warm-pool instances must complete bootstrap before entering the pool.
Key facts: Auto Scaling uses built-in EC2 status checks and any optional health checks enabled for the group.; When an InService instance is determined unhealthy, Auto Scaling replaces it to maintain desired capacity.; A launch lifecycle hook can hold an instance until startup work completes, before load balancer registration.; A termination lifecycle hook can pause an instance and send an EventBridge notification so work can run before termination.; A warm pool can stop or hibernate an entering instance without waiting for user data; an EC2_INSTANCE_LAUNCHING hook can hold it until bootstrap completes.
Gotchas: Attaching a load balancer does not, by itself, establish that its health checks are enabled as Auto Scaling health checks.; A health check grace period is not a substitute for holding an instance until bootstrap succeeds.; A termination hook does not prevent Spot interruption, and a timed-out termination hook proceeds with termination by default.
Confused with: 
ES: Un Auto Scaling group reemplaza las instancias que determina como no saludables, pero debes habilitar las comprobaciones de Elastic Load Balancing para el grupo si quieres que una falla detectada por el balanceador provoque el reemplazo. Usa lifecycle hooks para pausar el lanzamiento o la terminación mientras se completa una tarea; con un warm pool, un hook de lanzamiento puede evitar que la instancia se detenga o hibérne antes de terminar el bootstrap. Auto Scaling usa las comprobaciones integradas de estado de EC2 y las comprobaciones opcionales que habilites para el grupo.; Si determina que una instancia InService no está saludable, Auto Scaling la reemplaza para mantener la capacidad deseada.; Un launch lifecycle hook puede retener una instancia hasta que termine la preparación, antes de registrarla en el balanceador.; Un termination lifecycle hook puede pausar una instancia y enviar una notificación por EventBridge para ejecutar tareas antes de terminarla.; Un warm pool puede detener o hibernar una instancia sin esperar a que termine user data; un hook EC2_INSTANCE_LAUNCHING puede retenerla hasta completar el bootstrap.

chunks.title: ASG health checks, warm pools and lifecycle hooks
chunks.text:
Scenario: A ticketing company runs its web tier in an EC2 Auto Scaling group behind a load balancer. Some instances continue running but fail the load balancer's application health checks, leaving fewer instances able to serve requests. The company wants the group to replace those instances automatically while maintaining its desired capacity. Which change meets this requirement?
Correct: Enable Elastic Load Balancing health checks for the Auto Scaling group.
Why: The deciding requirement is replacement when an otherwise running instance fails the load balancer's application checks. Elastic Load Balancing is an optional health-check source for an Auto Scaling group; once enabled, a failed check can cause the group to replace an unhealthy InService instance. Increasing desired capacity adds instances without addressing the failing ones. Lifecycle hooks manage work during instance transitions, not which health signal triggers replacement.
Wrong options: Add a termination lifecycle hook that collects logs when the group scales in. (A termination hook runs before termination but does not supply the missing load balancer health signal.); Increase the group's desired capacity whenever the load balancer reports an unhealthy instance. (Adding capacity does not make the group determine that the failing instance is unhealthy and replace it.); Add a launch lifecycle hook that pauses each new instance until its application starts. (A launch hook controls startup work but does not make existing load-balancer-unhealthy instances eligible for replacement.)

chunks.title: ASG health checks, warm pools and lifecycle hooks
chunks.text:
Scenario: A media company launches rendering coordinators in an EC2 Auto Scaling group associated with a load balancer. Each new instance must download application packages and complete a configuration script before it can safely accept requests.
