Why: The agency needs to preserve SMB access, so FSx for Windows is the relevant managed file service. The excerpt identifies HDD storage as suited to home directories and departmental shares, while SSD targets more performance-sensitive workloads. SSD would retain compatibility but would provision a performance-oriented storage type without a stated need for it.
Wrong options: Use Amazon EFS and organize the files into home-directory folders. (EFS does not provide the Windows SMB interface the users must keep using.); Use Amazon FSx for Windows File Server with SSD storage. (SSD supports the SMB requirement but targets higher-performance, latency-sensitive workloads that this agency does not have.); Use Amazon S3 with a prefix for each department. (S3 object prefixes do not provide the existing SMB file-share interface.)

chunks.title: Gateway Load Balancer for third-party appliances
chunks.text:
Gateway Load Balancer for third-party appliances. Gateway Load Balancer (GWLB) inserts third-party virtual firewalls, IDS/IPS, and other inspection appliances transparently into network traffic. Choose it when traffic must pass through appliances without application-level routing, especially when the appliance fleet must scale with demand.
When to use: Traffic needs inline inspection by third-party virtual appliances.; The design needs a transparent entry and exit point for IP traffic across ports.; Applications in one VPC need private access to an appliance fleet in another VPC.
Key facts: GWLB operates at OSI Layer 3 and listens for IP packets across all ports.; GWLB exchanges application traffic with registered appliances using GENEVE on port 6081.; It routes traffic only to healthy registered targets and maintains flow stickiness; the default uses a 5-tuple.; For cross-VPC inspection, deploy GWLB with the appliances, create a GWLB endpoint in the consumer VPC, and direct traffic to the endpoint with route tables.; The GWLB endpoint and application servers must be in different subnets.
Gotchas: An ALB's HTTP routing is not a substitute for transparent inspection of IP traffic across ports.; An NLB can handle Layer 4 traffic, but it does not provide GWLB's transparent virtual-appliance insertion.; Creating a GWLB endpoint alone does not redirect application traffic; route tables must direct traffic through it.
Confused with: Application Load Balancer: Choose ALB for HTTP/HTTPS Layer 7 routing, not transparent inline appliance inspection.; Network Load Balancer: Choose NLB for TCP/UDP/TLS Layer 4 requirements; choose GWLB to insert and scale virtual security appliances.
ES: Gateway Load Balancer (GWLB) inserta de forma transparente firewalls virtuales, IDS/IPS y otros dispositivos de inspección de terceros en el tráfico de red. Elígelo cuando el tráfico deba pasar por esos dispositivos sin enrutamiento a nivel de aplicación, especialmente si necesitas escalar los dispositivos según la demanda. GWLB opera en la capa 3 del modelo OSI y recibe paquetes IP de todos los puertos.; GWLB intercambia tráfico de aplicación con los dispositivos registrados mediante GENEVE en el puerto 6081.; Envía tráfico solo a targets registrados que estén saludables y mantiene la afinidad de flujo; el valor predeterminado usa una 5-tuple.; Para inspección entre VPC, implementa GWLB junto a los dispositivos, crea un GWLB endpoint en la VPC consumidora y dirige el tráfico al endpoint mediante route tables.; El GWLB endpoint y los servidores de aplicación deben estar en subredes diferentes.

chunks.title: Gateway Load Balancer for third-party appliances
chunks.text:
Scenario: A media company is introducing a third-party IDS/IPS fleet to inspect traffic to several services. The services use different ports and protocols, and the security team wants a transparent inspection point that distributes traffic as appliance demand changes. Which load balancer should the company select?
Correct: Gateway Load Balancer with the IDS/IPS instances registered as targets.
Why: The deciding requirement is transparent distribution of traffic to an IDS/IPS fleet across different ports and protocols. GWLB listens for IP packets across all ports and scales distribution to virtual appliances as demand changes. NLB is a plausible choice for Layer 4 traffic, but the requirement is appliance insertion rather than a Layer 4 service front end. ALB's application-level routing also does not address that requirement.
Wrong options: Application Load Balancer with a separate target group for each IDS/IPS instance. (Separating ALB target groups does not provide GWLB's transparent network-gateway behavior.); Application Load Balancer with listener rules for each service's traffic. (ALB's application-level listener rules do not meet the need to inspect IP traffic across ports and protocols transparently.); Network Load Balancer with the IDS/IPS instances registered as targets. (NLB handles Layer 4 traffic but is not the load balancer designed for transparent virtual-appliance insertion.)

chunks.title: Gateway Load Balancer for third-party appliances
chunks.text:
Scenario: A manufacturing company runs application servers in a consumer VPC and virtual intrusion-prevention appliances in a provider VPC. It wants application-subnet traffic to traverse the appliances privately before returning to the consumer VPC, without changing application code. Which two actions are required for this design? (Choose two.)
Correct: Deploy a GWLB in the provider VPC and register the intrusion-prevention appliances in its target group. + Create a GWLB endpoint in a separate consumer-VPC subnet and configure the application subnet's route table to use it as the next hop.
Why: The company needs both an appliance-side distribution point and a consumer-side traffic path. Deploy GWLB with the appliances in the provider VPC, then create a GWLB endpoint in the consumer VPC and route application-subnet traffic to that endpoint. The endpoint must be in a different subnet from the application servers. An NLB cannot take the endpoint's place as the documented route-table next hop for this design.
Wrong options: Use an ALB in the consumer VPC to forward application requests to the provider VPC for inspection. (ALB application-level forwarding does not provide transparent appliance inspection for application-subnet traffic.); Use an NLB in the provider VPC as the next hop in the application subnet's route table. (The documented next hop for this cross-VPC inspection design is a GWLB endpoint, not an NLB.); Place the GWLB endpoint in the same subnet as the application servers. (The endpoint and application servers must be in different subnets.)

chunks.title: AWS Global Accelerator
chunks.text:
AWS Global Accelerator. AWS Global Accelerator provides fixed anycast entry points and carries traffic over the AWS global network to healthy regional endpoints. Choose it for global TCP/UDP applications that need static client-facing IPs, improved network performance, or fast regional failover without relying on DNS updates.
When to use: Clients or corporate firewalls must allow-list fixed IP addresses even when application endpoints move between Regions.; A non-HTTP application, such as a UDP game or IoT service, serves users globally.; A multi-Region application needs health-based routing to another Region without waiting for clients to refresh cached DNS answers.
Key facts: An IPv4 accelerator receives two static IPv4 addresses, anycast from the AWS edge network.; A standard accelerator can use Network Load Balancers, Application Load Balancers, EC2 instances, or Elastic IP addresses as regional endpoints.; Global Accelerator routes to endpoints based on health, client location, and configured policies; it can detect and remove an unhealthy endpoint in less than one minute.; Its static IP addresses remain assigned while the accelerator exists, including when it is disabled, but are lost if the accelerator is deleted.; Traffic dials control the percentage of traffic accepted by a regional endpoint group; endpoint weights control proportions within a group.
Gotchas: A DNS-based failover design may be affected by clients and resolvers that cache IP addresses for long periods.; Global Accelerator is not an edge cache; choose CloudFront when caching content is the deciding requirement.; A standard accelerator routes to healthy regional endpoints; a custom routing accelerator is for mapping users to specific destinations and uses VPC subnet endpoints.; Do not register an on-premises resource directly as a Global Accelerator endpoint.
Confused with: cloudfront-fundamentals: CloudFront serves web content through edge locations and can cache it; Global Accelerator provides static IP entry points and proxies TCP/UDP traffic to regional applications.; s3-transfer-acceleration: S3 Transfer Acceleration addresses long-distance uploads to an S3 bucket, not routing application connections among regional endpoints.
ES: AWS Global Accelerator ofrece puntos de entrada anycast con direcciones IP fijas y transporta el tráfico por la red global de AWS hacia endpoints regionales saludables. Elígelo para aplicaciones TCP/UDP globales que necesitan IP públicas estáticas, mejor rendimiento de red o failover regional rápido sin depender de actualizaciones de DNS. Un acelerador IPv4 recibe dos direcciones IPv4 estáticas, anunciadas mediante anycast desde la red de borde de AWS.; Un standard accelerator puede usar Network Load Balancers, Application Load Balancers, instancias EC2 o direcciones Elastic IP como endpoints regionales.; Global Accelerator dirige el tráfico según el estado de los endpoints, la ubicación del cliente y las políticas configuradas; puede detectar y retirar un endpoint no saludable en menos de un minuto.; Las IP estáticas siguen asignadas mientras exista el acelerador, incluso si está deshabilitado, pero se pierden al eliminarlo.; Los traffic dials controlan el porcentaje de tráfico que acepta un endpoint group regional; los pesos controlan la proporción de tráfico entre endpoints del grupo.

chunks.title: AWS Global Accelerator
chunks.text:
Scenario: A multiplayer game runs on Network Load Balancers in two AWS Regions and accepts UDP connections from players worldwide. The studio wants traffic to use the AWS global network and to move to healthy regional endpoints if one deployment fails. Which solution meets these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?
Correct: Create a standard AWS Global Accelerator and register the regional Network Load Balancers.
Why: The deciding requirements are UDP support, access to the AWS global network, and routing to healthy regional deployments. A standard Global Accelerator can direct TCP or UDP traffic to Network Load Balancers in multiple Regions and respond to endpoint health changes. CloudFront is a plausible global edge service, but it is not the fit for this UDP game. S3 Transfer Acceleration serves a different transfer workflow.
Wrong options: Place Amazon CloudFront in front of both regional deployments. (CloudFront is not the appropriate entry point for this UDP application.); Publish the addresses of both Network Load Balancers to players and have the game client test each address. (Client-side endpoint testing adds application work rather than providing managed global routing.); Enable S3 Transfer Acceleration for a bucket in each Region. (S3 Transfer Acceleration addresses transfers into S3 buckets, not UDP connections to the game.)

chunks.title: AWS Global Accelerator
chunks.text:
Scenario: A logistics company has a standard AWS Global Accelerator in front of a regional TCP service. Partners have allow-listed the accelerator's IPv4 addresses. The company is adding a second Region and replacing its original regional deployment, but partners must keep using their existing approved addresses while traffic can move to healthy endpoints. Which TWO actions meet these requirements? (Choose two.)
Correct: Add a regional endpoint group and register the second Region's Network Load Balancer with the existing accelerator. + Keep the existing accelerator and update its regional endpoints as the original deployment is replaced.
Why: Partners must keep the addresses already assigned to the accelerator while the company changes regional deployments. Adding the second Region's endpoint group to that accelerator enables multi-Region routing, and retaining the accelerator preserves its static IPs as endpoints change. Deleting it is the critical trap: assigned static addresses are lost on deletion. CloudFront and S3 Transfer Acceleration neither preserve those addresses nor meet this TCP routing requirement.
Wrong options: Replace the accelerator with S3 Transfer Acceleration for the second Region. (S3 Transfer Acceleration does not route TCP service traffic or preserve the approved accelerator IPs.); Delete the accelerator and create a replacement that includes endpoints in both Regions. (Deleting the accelerator forfeits its assigned static IP addresses, which partners have allow-listed.); Replace the accelerator with CloudFront distributions for each regional TCP endpoint. (This does not retain the accelerator IPs and does not fit the stated TCP entry-point requirement.)

chunks.title: AWS Global Accelerator
chunks.text:
Scenario: An IoT company hosts a TCP ingestion service on EC2 instances behind a Network Load Balancer in one AWS Region. Its devices are distributed worldwide, and the company wants fixed client-facing IP addresses and access to the AWS global network; a second Region may be added later. Which solution best meets these requirements?
Correct: Add the Network Load Balancer as an endpoint of a standard AWS Global Accelerator.
Why: Global Accelerator can benefit an application even when it currently runs in one Region. Its static anycast IPs let devices enter the AWS global network near them, and the company can later add regional endpoints without changing that public interface. A Network Load Balancer remains useful within the Region, but by itself does not supply the requested global entry. CloudFront and S3 Transfer Acceleration do not match this TCP ingestion workflow.
Wrong options: Use the regional Network Load Balancer as the sole public entry point. (A regional load balancer alone does not provide Global Accelerator's anycast entry onto the AWS global network.); Put CloudFront in front of the ingestion service as its global entry point. (CloudFront does not meet this non-HTTP TCP service's static-IP entry requirement.); Enable S3 Transfer Acceleration and send ingestion requests to an S3 bucket. (The service accepts TCP application connections rather than long-distance uploads to a bucket.)

chunks.title: AWS global infrastructure: Regions, AZs, edge locations
chunks.text:
AWS global infrastructure: Regions, AZs, edge locations. Choose a Region for geographic, legal, service-availability, and latency requirements. Use separate Availability Zones (AZs) within that Region to reduce exposure to an AZ failure; use another Region only when the requirements call for regional separation, and explicitly copy or replicate data there.
When to use: Users are concentrated in a particular geography and network latency matters.; Resources and data must remain in a specified geographic location.; A workload must withstand an AZ failure, or a separate copy must survive a regional failure.
Key facts: A Region contains multiple independent, physically separate AZs.; Regions are isolated and independent from one another, with some documented exceptions.; Resources and data created in one Region do not exist in another unless explicitly copied or replicated.; A Region introduced after March 20, 2019, must be enabled before it can be used.; Region selection should account for required service and feature availability.
Gotchas: Two AZs in one Region address AZ-level isolation, not the need for a copy in another Region.; Deploying in a second Region does not automatically put existing resources or data there.; A geographically suitable Region might require account opt-in before deployment.
Confused with: 
ES: Elige una Region según los requisitos geográficos, legales, de disponibilidad de servicios y de latencia. Usa Availability Zones (AZs) separadas dentro de esa Region para reducir el impacto de una falla de AZ; usa otra Region cuando necesites separación regional y copia o replica los datos explícitamente. Una Region contiene varias AZs independientes y físicamente separadas.; Las Regions están aisladas y son independientes entre sí, con algunas excepciones documentadas.; Los recursos y datos creados en una Region no aparecen en otra a menos que los copies o repliques explícitamente.; Debes habilitar una Region incorporada después del 20 de marzo de 2019 antes de usarla.; Al elegir una Region, verifica que tenga los servicios y features necesarios.

chunks.title: AWS global infrastructure: Regions, AZs, edge locations
chunks.text:
Scenario: A research organization runs an application in two Availability Zones in US East (Ohio). It now requires a separate copy of its research data that remains available for recovery if the entire Ohio Region is affected. Which change meets this requirement?
Correct: Explicitly copy or replicate the data to US West (Oregon).
Why: The new requirement concerns a failure affecting the whole Ohio Region, not just one AZ. A separate regional copy requires explicitly copying or replicating the data to another Region. Adding AZs in Ohio does not cross the regional boundary, and creating an empty deployment in Oregon does not transfer the data.
Wrong options: Create an application deployment in US West (Oregon) without copying the data. (Resources or data in Ohio do not appear in Oregon merely because a deployment is created there.); Add a third Availability Zone in US East (Ohio) for the application. (Another AZ remains within the Ohio Region and does not provide a separate regional copy.); Keep the two-AZ deployment and create another data copy in Ohio. (A second copy in Ohio does not meet the requirement for a copy outside that Region.)

chunks.title: AWS global infrastructure: Regions, AZs, edge locations
chunks.text:
Scenario: A ticketing company serves users primarily in Ireland. Its required AWS features are available in both Europe (Ireland) and Europe (Frankfurt). The company needs separation from an Availability Zone failure but wants to use as few Regions as possible while selecting a location close to most users. Which placement meets these requirements?
Correct: Deploy across two Availability Zones in Europe (Ireland).
Why: Both candidate Regions have the required features, so proximity to the primary users decides the Region choice. Two AZs in Ireland provide the requested AZ separation while using only one Region. A single Irish AZ misses the failure requirement; deploying in both Regions exceeds the stated placement need.
Wrong options: Deploy across two Availability Zones in Europe (Frankfurt). (This provides AZ separation in one Region but overlooks the closer Region for the primary users.); Deploy in one Availability Zone in Europe (Ireland). (The location is appropriate, but one AZ does not meet the AZ-failure requirement.); Deploy across two Availability Zones in each of Europe (Ireland) and Europe (Frankfurt). (This adds a second Region when the requirements explicitly call for using as few Regions as possible.)

chunks.title: AWS global infrastructure: Regions, AZs, edge locations
chunks.text:
Scenario: A Spanish retailer has selected Europe (Spain) because its new workload must run in Spain. The deployment team cannot create resources there because the Region is disabled in its AWS account. The required services are available in that Region. What should the team do to meet the location requirement?
Correct: Enable Europe (Spain) in the account, then deploy there.
Why: The workload must run in Spain, and the chosen Region is disabled in the account. Europe (Spain) is an opt-in Region, so the team must enable it before creating resources there. An enabled Region elsewhere does not meet the location requirement, and resources do not automatically appear across Regions.
Wrong options: Deploy in an additional Availability Zone in Europe (Frankfurt). (An AZ in Frankfurt remains in the Germany-based Region, not the Spain Region.); Deploy in Europe (Paris), which is enabled by default. (Paris being enabled does not satisfy the requirement to run the workload in Spain.); Create resources in Europe (Ireland) and wait for them to appear in Europe (Spain). (Resources created in Ireland do not automatically exist in Spain.)

chunks.title: AWS Glue ETL, crawlers and Data Catalog
chunks.text:
AWS Glue ETL, crawlers and Data Catalog. AWS Glue is a serverless service for discovering, cataloging, and transforming data. Choose crawlers to infer schemas, the Data Catalog to share metadata, and Glue ETL jobs to prepare data for analysis without managing infrastructure.
When to use: New or changing data sources need automatic schema discovery.; Analytics services need a central record of data locations and schemas.; Data must be cleaned or transformed before it is analyzed, with minimal infrastructure management.
Key facts: Crawlers scan data sources, extract metadata, and populate the AWS Glue Data Catalog.; The Data Catalog stores metadata such as data location and schema; it does not replace the underlying data store.; AWS Glue runs serverless ETL jobs, including Spark-based jobs.; Glue jobs can run on a schedule, on demand, or in response to an event.; Athena, Amazon EMR, and Amazon Redshift Spectrum can use cataloged data.
Gotchas: A crawler discovers metadata; it does not perform the data-cleaning work of an ETL job.; The Data Catalog holds metadata, not the source records themselves.; Athena can query cataloged S3 data, but querying is not a substitute for a required transformation pipeline.
Confused with: Amazon Athena: Athena queries S3 data with SQL; Glue discovers schemas, catalogs metadata, and runs ETL.; Amazon EMR: EMR fits processing that calls for control over big-data frameworks; Glue provides serverless ETL.; Amazon Redshift: Redshift is a data warehouse; the Glue Data Catalog is a shared metadata repository.
ES: AWS Glue es un servicio serverless para descubrir, catalogar y transformar datos. Elige crawlers para inferir esquemas, Data Catalog para compartir metadatos y trabajos de ETL de Glue para preparar datos sin administrar infraestructura. Los crawlers examinan las fuentes, extraen metadatos y completan AWS Glue Data Catalog.; Data Catalog almacena metadatos como la ubicación y el esquema; no reemplaza el almacén de datos subyacente.; AWS Glue ejecuta trabajos de ETL serverless, incluidos trabajos basados en Spark.; Puedes ejecutar trabajos de Glue según un horario, bajo demanda o a partir de un evento.; Athena, Amazon EMR y Amazon Redshift Spectrum pueden usar datos catalogados.

chunks.title: AWS Glue ETL, crawlers and Data Catalog
chunks.text:
Scenario: A healthcare organization collects records from several data sources. Before analysts use them, a nightly pipeline must clean and combine the records, and the team does not want to manage processing infrastructure. Which solution meets these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?
Correct: Schedule an AWS Glue ETL job to clean and combine the records.
Why: The records must be cleaned and combined before analysis, so schema discovery or queries alone are insufficient. AWS Glue runs ETL jobs on a schedule without infrastructure to manage. EMR is a plausible processing option, but it misses the scenario's minimal-management preference.
Wrong options: Run AWS Glue crawlers nightly to infer and catalog the source schemas. (Crawlers discover metadata but do not clean and combine the records.); Run the nightly transformations on an Amazon EMR cluster. (EMR can process data, but it does not match the stated preference for serverless ETL without infrastructure management.); Use Amazon Athena to query each source after the nightly files arrive. (Queries alone do not provide the required cleaning and combining pipeline.)

chunks.title: AWS Glue ETL, crawlers and Data Catalog
chunks.text:
Scenario: A manufacturer stores sensor exports in Amazon S3. Its analytics team already uses Athena, while a separate team plans to process the same data with Amazon EMR. New exports may introduce schema changes, and both teams need a shared metadata layer rather than separate definitions. Which solution meets these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?
Correct: Use AWS Glue crawlers to update Data Catalog tables that both analytics services can use.
Why: A changing schema and two analytics services point to automatic discovery and one shared metadata repository. Glue crawlers can update Data Catalog metadata, which Athena and EMR can use. Separate schema definitions fail the sharing requirement, while a warehouse would add an unnecessary loading step.
Wrong options: Load every export into Amazon Redshift and use its warehouse tables as the teams' shared definitions. (Loading data into a warehouse is unnecessary when the teams need shared metadata for existing S3 exports.); Create a Quick dashboard to display fields found in the latest sensor exports. (A visualization does not maintain shared table metadata for Athena and EMR.); Maintain the schema definitions independently in Athena and in the EMR processing jobs. (Independent definitions conflict with the requirement for a shared metadata layer.)

chunks.title: AWS Glue ETL, crawlers and Data Catalog
chunks.text:
Scenario: A logistics company receives files from new partners into Amazon S3. It must discover their schemas centrally and clean the incoming data before analysts query it; the team does not want to manage processing infrastructure. Which TWO actions meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead? (Choose two.)
Correct: Run AWS Glue crawlers to populate the Data Catalog with partner schemas. + Run AWS Glue ETL jobs to clean the data before analysis.
Why: This scenario has two distinct tasks: discover partner schemas and clean records before analysis. Glue crawlers populate the central Data Catalog, while Glue ETL jobs perform the cleaning without infrastructure to manage. Athena queries do not replace both tasks, and EMR does not best satisfy the management constraint.
Wrong options: Use Amazon Athena queries to identify fields in each incoming file. (Queries do not automatically maintain central schema metadata or perform the required cleaning pipeline.); Run Spark transformations on an Amazon EMR cluster before analysis. (EMR can transform data but does not match the preference to avoid managing processing infrastructure.); Load the incoming files into Amazon Redshift to establish the authoritative schemas. (Warehouse loading adds a data movement step instead of cataloging the incoming S3 sources.)

chunks.title: Governed provisioning: Service Catalog and License Manager
chunks.text:
Governed provisioning: Service Catalog and License Manager. AWS Service Catalog lets users self-provision approved IT products under organizational constraints. AWS License Manager tracks software license consumption and applies rules to help prevent licensing overages. Choose based on whether the requirement governs what users can deploy or how licenses are consumed.
When to use: Choose Service Catalog when users must discover and launch only approved products.; Choose Service Catalog when administrators must constrain product provisioning, such as launch location or instance type.; Choose License Manager when the organization must track BYOL usage or apply software license consumption limits across accounts and Regions.
Key facts: Service Catalog administrators organize products into portfolios, set constraints and provisioning tags, and grant portfolio access through IAM users and groups.; Service Catalog users can launch accessible products themselves as provisioned products without direct access to the underlying AWS services.; License Manager provides consolidated license visibility and reporting across multiple AWS accounts and Regions.; License Manager supports rule-based hard or soft limits on license consumption and tracks licenses measured by vCPUs, physical cores, sockets, or machines.
Gotchas: An approved deployment catalog does not, by itself, address software license consumption limits.; License Manager governs licenses; it is not the service for presenting users with a curated catalog of approved IT products.; IAM access alone does not provide Service Catalog's product listings and provisioning constraints.
Confused with: IAM access controls: IAM controls access; Service Catalog adds curated products that users can self-provision under product constraints.; AWS CloudFormation: A deployment template alone is not Service Catalog's portfolio-based discovery and governed self-service experience.
ES: AWS Service Catalog permite que los usuarios aprovisionen por sí mismos productos de TI aprobados, sujetos a restricciones de la organización. AWS License Manager registra el consumo de licencias de software y aplica reglas para ayudar a evitar excedentes. Elige según si necesitas gobernar qué pueden implementar los usuarios o cómo se consumen las licencias. En Service Catalog, los administradores organizan productos en portfolios, establecen restricciones y etiquetas de aprovisionamiento, y conceden acceso mediante usuarios y grupos de IAM.; Los usuarios pueden lanzar por sí mismos los productos a los que tienen acceso como provisioned products, sin acceso directo a los servicios de AWS subyacentes.; License Manager ofrece visibilidad y reportes consolidados de licencias entre varias cuentas de AWS y Regions.; License Manager admite límites hard o soft basados en reglas y registra licencias medidas por vCPUs, núcleos físicos, sockets o número de máquinas.

chunks.title: Governed provisioning: Service Catalog and License Manager
chunks.text:
Scenario: A university lets research teams request standard application environments. Teams must browse approved configurations and launch them without direct access to the underlying AWS services. Administrators also need to restrict which instance types each configuration can use. Which solution meets these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?
Correct: Publish the environments as AWS Service Catalog products with provisioning constraints.
Why: The deciding requirements are browsable approved configurations, self-service launch without direct access to underlying services, and instance-type restrictions. Service Catalog provides product listings and lets administrators apply provisioning constraints. Directly distributing templates misses the requested governed catalog experience.
Wrong options: Distribute approved AWS CloudFormation templates for teams to launch directly. (Templates alone do not provide Service Catalog's governed product listings and self-service launch experience.); Use AWS License Manager to publish the environments and set instance-type rules. (License Manager governs software licenses, not a catalog of launchable environments.); Give each team IAM access to launch instances that match an approved specification. (IAM access alone does not provide browsable, curated products with product-level provisioning constraints.)

chunks.title: Governed provisioning: Service Catalog and License Manager
chunks.text:
Scenario: A media company is moving servers covered by existing software licenses into several AWS accounts and Regions. Its compliance team needs consolidated usage reporting and rules that can stop deployments from exceeding its licensed capacity. Which solution meets these requirements?
Correct: Use AWS License Manager to track license usage and set rule-based consumption limits.
Why: The company must measure license use across accounts and Regions and apply limits before licensing overages occur. License Manager provides consolidated visibility and rule-based hard or soft limits on consumption. Service Catalog can govern which server products are offered, but that does not satisfy the license-usage requirement.
Wrong options: Use AWS Service Catalog to approve the server products users are allowed to launch. (Approving products does not provide consolidated license tracking or consumption limits.); Use IAM groups to limit which employees can launch the licensed servers. (Restricting launch access does not track software license consumption across accounts and Regions.); Use resource tags to identify licensed servers in each AWS account. (Tags can identify resources but do not themselves enforce license consumption limits.)

chunks.title: Amazon GuardDuty threat detection
chunks.text:
Amazon GuardDuty threat detection. Amazon GuardDuty detects suspicious and potentially malicious activity in AWS accounts. Choose it when a scenario calls for threat findings about compromised credentials or instances, rather than investigation of an existing finding or aggregation of findings.
When to use: Detect signs of compromised AWS credentials or unauthorized EC2 cryptomining.; Analyze CloudTrail management events, VPC flow logs from EC2 instances, and DNS logs without separately enabling those foundational sources for GuardDuty.; Extend detection to a specific workload, such as S3 or RDS, with the relevant GuardDuty protection plan.
Key facts: Enabling GuardDuty starts ingestion of its foundational sources: CloudTrail management events, VPC flow logs from EC2 instances, and DNS logs.; GuardDuty uses threat intelligence and machine learning to generate security findings.; S3 Protection identifies potential S3 data exfiltration and destruction attempts; RDS Protection analyzes supported RDS and Aurora login activity.; GuardDuty can create events for finding changes that Amazon EventBridge uses for near-real-time notification.
Gotchas: Foundational threat detection does not require separately enabling its three foundational data sources for GuardDuty.; A specialized protection plan is not interchangeable with foundational detection: Malware Protection for EC2 scans EBS volumes, while RDS Protection analyzes database logins.; Detective investigates findings; Security Hub CSPM aggregates and prioritizes findings. Neither replaces GuardDuty's threat detection.
Confused with: Amazon Detective: Use GuardDuty to detect potential threats; use Detective to investigate their nature and root cause.; AWS Security Hub CSPM: Security Hub CSPM consolidates findings and checks security posture; GuardDuty generates threat findings.; GuardDuty Malware Protection for EC2: It scans associated EBS volumes for malware; foundational GuardDuty detection analyzes account events and logs for suspicious activity.
ES: Amazon GuardDuty detecta actividad sospechosa y potencialmente maliciosa en cuentas de AWS. Elígelo cuando necesites hallazgos sobre credenciales o instancias comprometidas, en vez de investigar un hallazgo existente o reunir hallazgos de varios servicios. Al habilitar GuardDuty, comienza la ingesta de sus fuentes fundamentales: eventos de administración de CloudTrail, VPC flow logs de instancias EC2 y registros DNS.; GuardDuty usa inteligencia de amenazas y machine learning para generar hallazgos de seguridad.; S3 Protection identifica posibles intentos de exfiltración y destrucción de datos en S3; RDS Protection analiza la actividad de inicio de sesión en versiones compatibles de RDS y Aurora.; GuardDuty puede crear eventos cuando cambian los hallazgos, que Amazon EventBridge utiliza para notificaciones casi en tiempo real.

chunks.title: Amazon GuardDuty threat detection
chunks.text:
Scenario: A game studio already uses Amazon GuardDuty for its AWS accounts. Analysts receive findings about suspicious EC2 activity but spend too long establishing how related events fit together and what caused the incident. They do not need another source of initial threat findings or a cross-service compliance dashboard. Which service should they add to investigate the findings MOST effectively?
Correct: Amazon Detective, to analyze linked activity and help identify the root cause.
Why: GuardDuty is already producing the findings, so initial detection is not the gap. Detective helps analysts investigate findings by providing context and visualizations of related data to identify root cause. Security Hub CSPM can aggregate findings, but the scenario explicitly asks for investigation rather than a consolidated view.
Wrong options: AWS Security Hub CSPM, to aggregate and prioritize findings from security services. (Aggregation and prioritization do not meet the specific need to investigate how the events relate.); GuardDuty Malware Protection for EC2, to scan associated EBS volumes. (A malware scan does not investigate the relationships and root cause behind the existing findings.); Amazon EventBridge, to receive events when GuardDuty findings change. (Finding-change notifications do not provide the requested investigation of event relationships.)

chunks.title: Amazon GuardDuty threat detection
chunks.text:
Scenario: A regional retailer wants to detect suspicious activity involving AWS credentials and EC2 instances. Its operations team also needs to receive notifications soon after the resulting threat findings change so it can start its response workflow. Which solution meets both requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?
Correct: Enable Amazon GuardDuty and use Amazon EventBridge for finding-change notifications.
Why: This scenario requires both detection and timely notification, which are separate jobs. GuardDuty generates findings about potential threats, including compromised credentials and unauthorized EC2 activity. EventBridge can receive events when GuardDuty findings change, whereas Detective focuses on investigation after suspicious activity is identified.
Wrong options: Use Amazon Detective for detection and Security Hub CSPM for notifications. (Detective investigates activity rather than supplying the requested initial threat detection.); Use Security Hub CSPM for detection and Amazon Detective for notifications. (Security Hub CSPM aggregates findings rather than generating the requested GuardDuty threat findings.); Use GuardDuty Malware Protection for EC2 for detection and Detective for notifications. (EBS malware scanning is narrower than the requested credential and instance threat detection, and Detective is for investigation.)

chunks.title: Amazon GuardDuty threat detection
chunks.text:
Scenario: A clinic already uses GuardDuty's foundational threat detection for its EC2 environment. It now wants to identify unusual login patterns in supported Amazon RDS and Aurora databases that could indicate unauthorized access. The team wants to extend its existing threat detection rather than investigate findings that have already been produced. Which solution meets the new requirement MOST directly?
Correct: Enable the GuardDuty RDS Protection plan.
Why: The new signal is anomalous database login activity, not the foundational sources used for EC2-oriented detection. GuardDuty RDS Protection is the dedicated plan that analyzes and profiles login activity for supported RDS and Aurora databases. Detective would help investigate suspicious activity, but it does not add this requested detection source.
Wrong options: Keep foundational GuardDuty detection unchanged and review its EC2 VPC flow log findings. (EC2 VPC flow log analysis does not provide the specified profiling of supported database login activity.); Enable GuardDuty Malware Protection for EC2 to scan EBS volumes. (Scanning EC2-associated EBS volumes does not analyze RDS or Aurora login patterns.); Add Amazon Detective to investigate related log data. (Detective helps investigate findings rather than adding the requested database-login threat detection.)

chunks.title: AWS Health Dashboard and Trusted Advisor checks
chunks.text:
AWS Health Dashboard and Trusted Advisor checks. Use AWS Trusted Advisor to inspect your environment for best-practice opportunities involving cost, security, availability, performance, and service limits. Use the AWS Health Dashboard when you need to know about AWS events or planned activities that could affect your services or resources.
When to use: Choose Trusted Advisor for checks and recommendations about your AWS environment.; Choose AWS Health Dashboard for an AWS event affecting your resources or for visibility into planned AWS activities.; Check the support plan when a scenario requires access to all Trusted Advisor checks.
Key facts: Trusted Advisor inspects AWS environments and recommends ways to save money, improve availability or performance, and close security gaps.; Business Support+, Enterprise Support, and Unified Operations plans provide access to all Trusted Advisor checks.; Basic Support provides all Service Limits checks and selected Security and Fault tolerance checks, but not automatic check updates.; AWS Health Dashboard requires no setup, is available to all AWS customers, and has no additional cost.
Gotchas: A best-practice finding is not the same as an AWS Health event affecting a resource.; Basic Support does not provide access to every Trusted Advisor check.; Do not choose a spending-analysis tool when the requirement is to inspect the environment for security or availability gaps.
Confused with: AWS Cost Explorer: Choose it to visualize or forecast spending; choose Trusted Advisor for best-practice checks.; AWS Compute Optimizer: Choose it for utilization-based rightsizing recommendations; choose Trusted Advisor for broader best-practice checks.; AWS Health Dashboard: It reports AWS events and planned activities that may affect resources, rather than inspecting your environment for best-practice opportunities.
ES: Usa AWS Trusted Advisor para revisar tu entorno y encontrar oportunidades basadas en mejores prácticas de costos, seguridad, disponibilidad, rendimiento y límites de servicio. Usa AWS Health Dashboard cuando necesites conocer eventos de AWS o actividades planificadas que puedan afectar tus servicios o recursos. Trusted Advisor inspecciona los entornos de AWS y recomienda oportunidades para ahorrar dinero, mejorar la disponibilidad o el rendimiento y reducir brechas de seguridad.; Los planes Business Support+, Enterprise Support y Unified Operations dan acceso a todas las verificaciones de Trusted Advisor.; Basic Support incluye todas las verificaciones de Service Limits y algunas de Security y Fault tolerance, pero no actualiza automáticamente las verificaciones.; AWS Health Dashboard no requiere configuración, está disponible para todos los clientes de AWS y no tiene costo adicional.

chunks.title: AWS Health Dashboard and Trusted Advisor checks
chunks.text:
Scenario: A media company with Business Support+ is preparing a quarterly architecture review. The team wants one AWS service to inspect its environment for opportunities to reduce waste, close security gaps, and improve availability; it does not need a spending forecast. Which solution meets these requirements?
Correct: Use AWS Trusted Advisor to review its checks.
Why: The team needs an inspection of its environment across several best-practice areas, not a report of AWS events or a forecast of spending. Trusted Advisor makes recommendations about saving money, closing security gaps, and improving availability. The stated Business Support+ plan provides access to all Trusted Advisor checks. AWS Health Dashboard is the key distractor because it addresses AWS events rather than this architecture review.
Wrong options: Use AWS Compute Optimizer to review rightsizing recommendations. (Rightsizing recommendations do not cover the requested security and availability checks.); Use AWS Health Dashboard to review account events. (AWS Health reports events, not best-practice opportunities across cost, security, and availability.); Use AWS Cost Explorer to review spending trends. (Spending trends do not provide the requested cross-category environment checks.)

chunks.title: AWS Health Dashboard and Trusted Advisor checks
chunks.text:
Scenario: A research laboratory with Enterprise Support is dividing its cloud operations work into two streams. One stream must identify AWS events that may affect its running resources; the other must inspect the AWS environment for best-practice opportunities involving cost, security, and availability. Which two services together meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead? (Choose two.)
Correct: AWS Trusted Advisor + AWS Health Dashboard
Why: These are two different operational needs. AWS Health Dashboard covers AWS events that may affect resources and requires no setup, while Trusted Advisor inspects the environment for best-practice opportunities. The laboratory's Enterprise Support plan provides access to all Trusted Advisor checks. A spending or rightsizing tool cannot replace both event visibility and the requested cross-category checks.
Wrong options: AWS Cost Explorer (Spending analysis does not identify AWS Health events or inspect the environment across all three requested areas.); AWS Compute Optimizer (Rightsizing recommendations do not satisfy the event or cross-category best-practice requirements.); AWS Budgets (Budget thresholds do not identify resource-affecting AWS events or perform the requested best-practice inspection.)

chunks.title: Horizontal vs vertical scaling
chunks.text:
Horizontal vs vertical scaling. Horizontal scaling adds or removes instances; vertical scaling changes the capacity of an instance. For a stateless workload with changing demand, favor automated scale-out and scale-in. For a workload that must remain on one instance, consider resizing if a maintenance window is acceptable.
When to use: Choose horizontal scaling when requests can be handled by interchangeable instances and demand fluctuates.; Choose horizontal scaling across multiple locations when the workload must remain available after an instance or location failure.; Consider vertical scaling when the component cannot run across multiple instances and a larger instance meets its needs.
Key facts: Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling can automatically provision or deprovision instances according to metrics and scaling policies.; Scale-out adds capacity; scale-in removes capacity when it is no longer needed.; A load balancer can distribute requests across instances in an Auto Scaling group.; Deploying across multiple fault-isolation boundaries reduces the impact of a failure.; Scheduled scaling suits predictable usage patterns; metric-based policies can respond to changing demand.
Gotchas: Adding instances does not help a component whose work cannot be shared among instances.; Making one instance larger does not provide another serving instance if that instance fails.; A permanently oversized fleet can meet peak demand but does not remove unneeded capacity when demand falls.
Confused with: 
ES: El escalamiento horizontal agrega o elimina instancias; el vertical cambia la capacidad de una instancia. Para una carga sin estado cuya demanda varía, prefiere scale-out y scale-in automáticos. Si la carga debe permanecer en una sola instancia, considera cambiar su tamaño cuando se permita una ventana de mantenimiento. Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling puede aprovisionar o retirar instancias automáticamente según métricas y políticas de escalamiento.; Scale-out agrega capacidad; scale-in la retira cuando ya no se necesita.; Un load balancer puede distribuir solicitudes entre las instancias de un Auto Scaling group.; Desplegar en varios límites de aislamiento reduce el impacto de una falla.; Scheduled scaling sirve para patrones predecibles; las políticas basadas en métricas pueden responder a cambios en la demanda.

chunks.title: Horizontal vs vertical scaling
chunks.text:
Scenario: A manufacturing team runs a legacy calculation service on one EC2 instance. Its jobs depend on process state held locally, and the team cannot change the software to distribute a job across instances this quarter. Memory demand has risen steadily, and the team has an approved maintenance window. Which approach meets the immediate requirement with the LEAST application change?
Correct: Move the service to an EC2 instance size with sufficient memory during the maintenance window.
Why: The binding constraint is that the service must process a job with local state on one instance. Increasing that instance's memory capacity addresses the immediate need without rewriting the application, and the maintenance window accommodates the change. Adding instances—even behind a load balancer or on a schedule—does not make the existing job distributable.
Wrong options: Put multiple copies of the service behind an Application Load Balancer and route jobs to any copy. (Routing to another copy does not make the job's locally held process state available there.); Use scheduled scaling to start more service instances during the daily calculation period. (A predictable schedule does not solve the software's inability to share a calculation job.); Add instances to an EC2 Auto Scaling group and distribute each calculation job among them. (The current software cannot distribute a job or its local process state among instances.)

chunks.title: Horizontal vs vertical scaling
chunks.text:
Scenario: A media company processes independent thumbnail requests on EC2 instances. Demand varies sharply throughout the week, and requests can run on any instance. The company wants enough capacity during busy periods without paying for the same fleet size during quiet periods. Which solution meets these requirements MOST cost-effectively?
Correct: Use an EC2 Auto Scaling group with metric-based scale-out and scale-in policies.
Why: Because requests are independent and can run on any instance, the workload can use horizontal scaling. Metric-based EC2 Auto Scaling adds capacity as demand rises and removes it when demand falls, supporting the cost requirement. A permanently peak-sized instance or fleet keeps excess capacity during quiet periods.
Wrong options: Run one EC2 instance sized for the highest expected request volume. (Peak-sized capacity remains provisioned during quiet periods and leaves one serving instance.); Increase each instance's size during busy periods while keeping the fleet count fixed. (Repeatedly changing instance sizes does not use automatic scale-out and scale-in to track variable demand.); Keep a fixed fleet of EC2 instances sized for the highest expected request volume. (A fixed fleet retains peak capacity even when the request volume drops.)

chunks.title: Choosing Direct Connect vs VPN vs internet by cost
chunks.text:
Choosing Direct Connect vs VPN vs internet by cost. Choose connectivity by matching the traffic pattern and network requirement to the total quoted cost. Site-to-Site VPN can reuse an existing internet connection for intermittent private connectivity; Direct Connect can justify a dedicated circuit when sustained transfer makes its bandwidth savings worthwhile.
When to use: An on-premises network needs private connectivity to resources in a VPC.; Traffic volume is low or variable, and an existing internet connection can be reused.; Traffic is sustained enough to evaluate a dedicated circuit against its recurring charges and expected transfer savings.
Key facts: AWS Site-to-Site VPN provides an AWS-managed IPsec connection over the internet.; Site-to-Site VPN can reuse existing internet connections and VPN equipment.; AWS Direct Connect provides a dedicated connection over private lines, with more predictable network performance and reduced bandwidth costs.; Direct Connect might require new circuits or additional telecom and hosting provider relationships.; VPN latency, variability, and availability depend on internet conditions.
Gotchas: Reduced bandwidth costs do not, by themselves, make Direct Connect the lowest-total-cost choice; compare them with the quoted recurring connection and circuit costs.; Do not choose ordinary public internet access when the requirement is to extend an internal network to private VPC resources.; An AWS-managed VPN service does not remove the need to plan redundancy and failover when required.
Confused with: Public internet access: It fits a public endpoint, but does not provide the IPsec network extension specified for private VPC access.; Software VPN: It supports a wider range of vendors and protocols but is fully customer-managed.
ES: Elige la conectividad según el patrón de tráfico, el requisito de red y el costo total cotizado. Site-to-Site VPN puede reutilizar una conexión a internet para conectividad privada intermitente; Direct Connect puede justificar un circuito dedicado cuando el tráfico sostenido compensa su costo con ahorros de transferencia. AWS Site-to-Site VPN proporciona una conexión IPsec administrada por AWS a través de internet.; Site-to-Site VPN puede reutilizar conexiones a internet y equipos VPN existentes.; AWS Direct Connect proporciona una conexión dedicada por líneas privadas, con rendimiento de red más predecible y menores costos de ancho de banda.; Direct Connect podría requerir circuitos nuevos o relaciones adicionales con proveedores de telecomunicaciones y alojamiento.; La latencia, la variabilidad y la disponibilidad de VPN dependen de las condiciones de internet.

chunks.title: Choosing Direct Connect vs VPN vs internet by cost
chunks.text:
Scenario: A research organization is selecting separate connections for two sites. A field station needs IPsec access to private VPC resources, sends data irregularly, and can reuse its existing internet connection; its quoted private circuit would not pay for itself. A processing center transfers data steadily, and its quoted private-line bandwidth savings exceed its recurring connection and provider charges. Which two choices meet the sites' requirements MOST cost-effectively? (Choose two.)
Correct: Use AWS Direct Connect over a private line for the processing center. + Use AWS Site-to-Site VPN over the field station's existing internet connection.
Why: The sites have different transfer patterns, so a single connectivity choice is not necessarily cost-effective for both. Site-to-Site VPN gives the field station IPsec access using its existing internet connection, while its proposed private circuit would not pay for itself. Direct Connect fits the processing center because its quoted bandwidth savings exceed the recurring private-line charges. VPN at the processing center would forgo those modeled savings.
Wrong options: Use AWS Site-to-Site VPN over the internet for the processing center. (It misses the processing center's modeled net savings from using the quoted private line.); Use AWS Direct Connect for the field station's private VPC access. (The field station's quoted circuit costs are not offset by its irregular transfers.); Use ordinary public internet access for the field station's private VPC resources. (Public access alone does not provide the station's required IPsec connectivity.)

chunks.title: Choosing Direct Connect vs VPN vs internet by cost
chunks.text:
Scenario: A small publisher occasionally sends files from its office network to an application in a VPC. The application must remain accessible through an IPsec connection from the office, and the publisher can reuse its existing internet connection and VPN equipment. Its circuit quote would add recurring costs that its infrequent transfers would not offset. Which solution meets these requirements MOST cost-effectively?
Correct: Connect the office to the VPC with AWS Site-to-Site VPN over the existing internet connection.
Why: The deciding constraints are IPsec connectivity and infrequent transfers that do not offset the quoted circuit costs. AWS Site-to-Site VPN uses the existing internet connection and can reuse existing VPN equipment. Direct Connect offers bandwidth-cost benefits, but those benefits do not make the proposed circuit cost-effective for this publisher.
Wrong options: Expose the application to the office over the public internet without a VPN. (Ordinary internet access does not meet the stated IPsec connection requirement.); Provision AWS Direct Connect over a new private circuit for the office. (Its dedicated circuit adds the quoted recurring costs without enough transfer savings in this scenario.); Deploy a software VPN appliance in the VPC and connect the office over the internet. (A software VPN adds customer-managed operations without a stated need for its broader protocol support.)

chunks.title: IAM identity-based policies and least privilege
chunks.text:
IAM identity-based policies and least privilege. An IAM identity-based policy grants an IAM user, group, or role permission to perform actions on resources, optionally under specified conditions. For least privilege, choose the required actions and resources rather than granting broad access or relying on a policy that only sets a permissions ceiling.
When to use: A user, group, or workload role needs permission to perform specific tasks.; Several identities need the same reusable, narrowly scoped permissions.; An existing identity policy grants more access than the task requires.
Key facts: Identity-based policies are JSON documents attached to users, groups, or roles; they specify actions, resources, and optional conditions.; A customer managed policy can be attached to multiple identities and provides more precise control for a use case than a general AWS managed policy.; An inline policy belongs to one identity and is deleted with that identity.; IAM Access Analyzer can generate a fine-grained policy from access activity logged in AWS CloudTrail; test it before deployment.; A permissions boundary and an SCP limit permissions but do not grant them.
Gotchas: Attaching a broad AWS managed policy may work but may not provide least privilege for the workload.; A permissions boundary cannot replace an identity-based policy that grants the required actions.; A cross-account resource policy naming a principal is only half of the access arrangement; the principal also needs an identity-based policy.
Confused with: Resource-based policy: It attaches to a resource and grants access to a specified principal; an identity-based policy attaches to a user, group, or role.; Service control policy (SCP): It caps permissions in an organization or OU but grants no permissions.; Permissions boundary: It caps what identity-based policies can grant to a particular IAM user or role but grants no permissions itself.
ES: Una IAM identity-based policy concede a un usuario, grupo o rol de IAM permiso para realizar acciones sobre recursos, opcionalmente bajo condiciones específicas. Para aplicar least privilege, elige solo las acciones y los recursos necesarios; no dependas de una política que únicamente establezca un límite máximo. Las identity-based policies son documentos JSON adjuntos a usuarios, grupos o roles; especifican acciones, recursos y condiciones opcionales.; Puedes adjuntar una customer managed policy a varias identidades y ajustarla mejor a un caso de uso que una AWS managed policy general.; Una inline policy pertenece a una sola identidad y se elimina junto con ella.; IAM Access Analyzer puede generar una política detallada a partir de la actividad registrada en AWS CloudTrail; pruébala antes de implementarla.; Una permissions boundary y una SCP limitan permisos, pero no los conceden.

chunks.title: IAM identity-based policies and least privilege
chunks.text:
Scenario: A research lab stores a dataset in an Amazon S3 bucket in its AWS account. An IAM role in a partner's separate AWS account needs access to only that dataset; the lab can update the bucket policy, and the partner can update the role's permissions. Which solution grants the required cross-account access with the MOST narrowly scoped permissions?
Correct: Grant the partner role access to the dataset in the bucket policy and in the role's identity-based policy.
Why: The accounts are separate, so the partner role needs both sides of this access arrangement. The lab's bucket policy can grant the specified cross-account principal access to the dataset, and the partner's identity-based policy must also grant the role access. Either policy alone misses a required side of the arrangement; SCPs grant no access.
Wrong options: Allow the dataset in an SCP in the lab's account and an SCP in the partner's account. (SCPs limit permissions but do not grant access to the partner role or name it as an allowed bucket principal.); Grant the partner role access to the dataset in its identity-based policy without changing the bucket policy. (The partner role's identity policy alone does not establish the resource-side cross-account permission described.); Add the partner role to the bucket policy and make no changes to the partner role's identity-based policy. (For this cross-account access, the partner principal also needs an identity-based policy granting access.)

chunks.title: IAM identity-based policies and least privilege
chunks.text:
Scenario: A software company lets a platform team create IAM roles in one AWS account. The team must be able to grant each new role only the actions needed by its workload, but must not be able to give those roles permissions beyond a company-approved maximum. Which TWO policy measures meet these requirements? (Choose two.)
Correct: Attach an identity-based policy to each new role granting only its workload's required actions. + Apply a permissions boundary to each new role containing the company-approved maximum permissions.
Why: Each role needs a task-specific grant and a separate ceiling on what that grant can include. Its identity-based policy supplies the required workload actions, while a permissions boundary limits the maximum permissions those identity-based policies can grant. An SCP cannot act as the sole grant, and a role's resource-based trust policy addresses who can assume it rather than its workload permissions.
Wrong options: Attach a resource-based policy to each new role that lists the maximum workload actions. (A role trust policy controls assumption of the role and does not serve as its maximum-permissions boundary.); Use an SCP as the sole policy on the account to grant each new role its workload actions. (An SCP can limit account permissions but cannot grant actions to the new roles.); Attach a resource-based policy to each new role that lists the workload actions it may perform. (A role's resource-based trust policy determines who can assume it, not which workload actions its identity can perform.)

chunks.title: IAM identity-based policies and least privilege
chunks.text:
Scenario: A media company runs a processing workload on Amazon EC2. The workload needs to read only its assigned objects in an Amazon S3 bucket, and the team does not want to distribute long-term credentials to the instances. Which solution meets these requirements with the MOST secure permissions?
Correct: Use an IAM role for the EC2 workload with an identity-based policy allowing only the required read actions on its assigned objects.
Why: The workload needs temporary credentials and narrowly scoped access to its assigned objects. An EC2 workload can use an IAM role, and an identity-based policy on that role can grant the required actions on the specified resources. A permissions boundary or SCP cannot supply the missing grant; IAM user access keys also fail the credential requirement.
Wrong options: Attach a permissions boundary allowing reads of the assigned objects to the EC2 workload role. (A permissions boundary limits identity-based grants but does not itself grant the workload read access.); Give the workload IAM user access keys and attach a policy allowing access to every object in the bucket. (Long-term IAM user credentials are unnecessary for an EC2 workload, and access to every object exceeds the stated need.); Attach an SCP allowing reads of the assigned objects to the workload's AWS account. (An SCP sets a permissions ceiling for an account but does not grant the workload permission to read objects.)

chunks.title: AWS IAM Identity Center (workforce SSO)
chunks.text:
AWS IAM Identity Center (workforce SSO). IAM Identity Center centralizes workforce access to AWS accounts and applications. For access across multiple AWS accounts, choose an organization instance; use permission sets when teams need centrally defined job-function permissions.
When to use: Employees need one access portal for assigned AWS accounts and applications.; An organization needs to manage workforce access across multiple AWS accounts.; Teams want to connect an existing identity provider without federating it separately for each account.
Key facts: IAM Identity Center can use an existing identity provider and synchronized directory users and groups, or users managed directly in IAM Identity Center.; An organization instance is the only instance type that supports managing access to AWS accounts.; Organization instances can use permission sets to create job-function permissions centrally and provision them across accounts.; IAM Identity Center can centrally assign users and groups to IAM roles that teams create in their accounts.; The AWS access portal shows users their assigned applications and AWS accounts.
Gotchas: An account instance does not manage access to AWS accounts; it supports isolated deployments of select AWS managed applications.; Permission sets are not mandatory if teams want to retain IAM roles created in their accounts.; Using IAM Identity Center for applications does not require replacing an existing IAM federation workflow for account access.
Confused with: SAML/OIDC federation to IAM roles: Direct IAM federation can remain in place, but IAM Identity Center offers one point of federation and central management across multiple AWS accounts.; AWS Directory Service: A directory can supply workforce identities; IAM Identity Center manages their access to assigned AWS accounts and applications.; Amazon Cognito user pools: IAM Identity Center targets workforce access to AWS accounts and applications, rather than customer sign-in to an application.
ES: IAM Identity Center centraliza el acceso del personal a cuentas de AWS y aplicaciones. Para gestionar el acceso entre varias cuentas de AWS, elige una instancia de organización; usa permission sets cuando los equipos necesiten permisos por función laboral definidos de forma central. IAM Identity Center puede usar un proveedor de identidad existente y usuarios y grupos sincronizados desde un directorio, o usuarios administrados directamente en IAM Identity Center.; La instancia de organización es el único tipo de instancia que permite gestionar el acceso a cuentas de AWS.; Las instancias de organización pueden usar permission sets para definir permisos por función laboral de forma central y aprovisionarlos en varias cuentas.; IAM Identity Center puede asignar de forma central usuarios y grupos a roles de IAM que los equipos creen en sus cuentas.; El AWS access portal muestra a los usuarios las aplicaciones y cuentas de AWS que tienen asignadas.

chunks.title: AWS IAM Identity Center (workforce SSO)
chunks.text:
Scenario: A manufacturing company is consolidating employee access to AWS accounts acquired with several subsidiaries. Employees should see their assigned accounts in one portal, and administrators must define common job-function permissions centrally and provision them across those accounts. Which TWO components should the company use? (Choose two.)
Correct: An IAM Identity Center organization instance for workforce access to AWS accounts. + IAM Identity Center permission sets assigned to the relevant workforce users and groups.
Why: The company needs both central AWS account access and common permissions defined across accounts. An IAM Identity Center organization instance provides account-access management and an access portal; permission sets provide centrally managed job-function permissions. Account instances cannot manage AWS account access, and separate per-account configurations miss the central-management requirement.
Wrong options: Separate IAM federation configurations in each account for common job-function permissions. (Separate account configurations do not meet the requirement to define and provision permissions centrally.); IAM users created independently in each account for employees to select from the access portal. (Per-account IAM users do not provide the requested central workforce assignments through the access portal.); An IAM Identity Center account instance in each subsidiary account for workforce account access. (Account instances do not support managing access to AWS accounts.)

chunks.title: AWS IAM Identity Center (workforce SSO)
chunks.text:
Scenario: A logistics company is adding AWS accounts for regional teams. Employees need a portal for their assigned accounts, and administrators want to define the same job-function permissions centrally rather than maintain them in each account. Which solution meets these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?
Correct: Create an IAM Identity Center organization instance and assign centrally managed permission sets to users and groups.
Why: The deciding requirements are a portal for multiple accounts and centrally defined job-function permissions. An IAM Identity Center organization instance supports AWS account access, and its permission sets can be provisioned across accounts and assigned to users and groups. An account instance cannot manage AWS account access, while separate federation leaves account-level administration in place.
Wrong options: Federate the company's identity provider separately with IAM in each regional account. (Separate account federation does not provide the requested central management of job-function permissions.); Create IAM users in each regional account and give employees links to the account sign-in pages. (Per-account users and sign-in pages do not provide the requested central assignments and access portal.); Create an IAM Identity Center account instance and define permission sets for the regional accounts. (An account instance cannot manage access to AWS accounts.)

chunks.title: AWS IAM Identity Center (workforce SSO)
chunks.text:
Scenario: A media company already uses a SAML 2.0 identity provider for its employees. It is expanding to several AWS accounts and AWS managed applications, and the security team wants to retain that identity provider while avoiding a separate federation configuration for each destination. Which approach meets these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?
Correct: Connect the identity provider to an IAM Identity Center organization instance and manage workforce assignments centrally.
Why: Retaining the SAML 2.0 identity provider while avoiding federation at each destination points to IAM Identity Center. An organization instance supports managing access to AWS accounts and can also serve application access. Federating independently with every account misses the single-federation requirement; account instances cannot manage account access.
Wrong options: Create an IAM Identity Center account instance for each account and connect each one to the identity provider. (Account instances do not manage AWS account access and would not provide the requested single point.); Create employees directly in IAM Identity Center and stop using the existing identity provider. (Directly managed users would not retain the required existing identity provider.); Federate the SAML 2.0 identity provider independently with each AWS account and configure application access separately. (Independent configurations do not meet the requirement for one point of federation.)

chunks.title: IAM policy conditions (SourceIp, PrincipalOrgID, MFA, tags)
chunks.text:
IAM policy conditions (SourceIp, PrincipalOrgID, MFA, tags). IAM policy conditions compare request context with values in a policy to determine when a permission applies. Choose the key that matches the requirement—organization membership, network origin, MFA authentication, tags, or requested Region—rather than redesigning access around a different identity or network.
When to use: Access should follow accounts as they join or leave an AWS organization.; A permission should apply only when a request comes through a specified VPC endpoint or from an approved IP range.; An action requires MFA, a matching principal tag, or a specified requested Region.
Key facts: aws:PrincipalOrgID matches the requesting principal’s AWS Organizations ID; it avoids maintaining an account ID list as membership changes.; aws:SourceIp and aws:SourceVpce are network-related condition keys; choose the one that matches the network property the requirement specifies.; aws:MultiFactorAuthPresent can test whether MFA is present in the request context.; aws:PrincipalTag/tag-key tests a tag on an IAM user, role, or role session; aws:ResourceTag/tag-key tests a resource tag where supported.; A condition key missing from a request normally does not match. An IfExists condition can instead return true when its key is missing.
Gotchas: aws:PrincipalOrgID identifies the requester’s organization, not an individual AWS account.; An organization-only condition can also exclude AWS service principals that need access to a resource.; Do not use an IfExists operator when a missing MFA context must fail the condition.; Do not use wildcards with sensitive keys such as aws:PrincipalOrgID or aws:SourceVpce.
Confused with: aws:PrincipalAccount: Matches an account ID, whereas aws:PrincipalOrgID follows organization membership as accounts change.; aws:ResourceTag/tag-key: Tests a resource’s tag, whereas aws:PrincipalTag/tag-key tests the requester’s tag.
ES: Las condiciones de una política IAM comparan el contexto de la solicitud con los valores de la política para determinar cuándo se aplica un permiso. Elige la clave que corresponda al requisito —organización, origen de red, MFA, etiquetas o Region solicitada— sin rediseñar la arquitectura de acceso. aws:PrincipalOrgID compara el ID de la organización del principal solicitante; evita mantener una lista de IDs de cuentas cuando cambia la membresía.; aws:SourceIp y aws:SourceVpce son claves relacionadas con la red; elige la que corresponda a la propiedad de red requerida.; aws:MultiFactorAuthPresent permite comprobar si MFA está presente en el contexto de la solicitud.; aws:PrincipalTag/tag-key comprueba una etiqueta de un usuario, rol o sesión de rol; aws:ResourceTag/tag-key comprueba una etiqueta del recurso cuando el servicio la admite.; Por lo general, una clave ausente del contexto de la solicitud no coincide. En cambio, una condición IfExists puede devolver true si falta la clave.

chunks.title: IAM policy conditions (SourceIp, PrincipalOrgID, MFA, tags)
chunks.text:
Scenario: A publishing company allows employees in its AWS organization to upload files to a shared S3 bucket. New AWS accounts join the organization regularly, and the bucket policy must not need an account ID update each time. The uploads are made by employee principals, not AWS service principals. Which condition should the company use to meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?
Correct: Match aws:PrincipalOrgID against the company’s AWS Organizations ID.
Why: The deciding requirement is that authorization must track organization membership as accounts are added without policy edits. aws:PrincipalOrgID compares the requester’s organization ID and avoids maintaining an account ID list. aws:PrincipalAccount could identify member accounts, but its list would need maintenance. The scenario excludes AWS service principals because an organization-only condition can prevent their access.
Wrong options: Match aws:PrincipalAccount against a maintained list of member account IDs. (The account list must be updated when organization membership changes.); Match aws:PrincipalOrgPaths against the path of one organizational unit. (A condition restricted to one organizational unit would not cover the stated organization-wide access requirement.); Match aws:PrincipalTag/department against a company department value. (A department tag does not establish that the requester belongs to the company’s organization.)

chunks.title: IAM policy conditions (SourceIp, PrincipalOrgID, MFA, tags)
chunks.text:
Scenario: A research institute assigns department tags to IAM role sessions. It wants a policy permission to apply only when the requesting session has department=imaging and the request targets the institute’s approved AWS Region. The policy must test both properties of the request. Which two condition keys meet these requirements? (Choose two.)
Correct: aws:RequestedRegion + aws:PrincipalTag/department
Why: The permission depends on two separate request properties: the principal’s session tag and the requested Region. aws:PrincipalTag/department addresses the first, and aws:RequestedRegion addresses the second. aws:ResourceTag/department is tempting but tests the resource rather than the requester. The other keys test network origin or organization membership, neither of which is a stated requirement.
Wrong options: aws:SourceIp (The source IP does not identify either the session’s department tag or the requested Region.); aws:PrincipalOrgID (Organization membership does not test the session tag or the requested Region.); aws:ResourceTag/department (This tests a resource tag rather than the requesting role session’s department tag.)

chunks.title: IAM policy evaluation logic (explicit deny wins)
chunks.text:
IAM policy evaluation logic (explicit deny wins). IAM evaluates the policies that apply to a request, and an explicit deny overrides any allow. For exam scenarios, identify the policy types in scope before deciding whether permissions combine as a union or an intersection.
When to use: A request has an allow in one policy but a deny in another.; A same-account request involves identity-based and resource-based policies.; A user's permissions boundary or an AWS Organizations SCP limits an otherwise allowed action.
Key facts: For an IAM user or role accessing a resource in the same account, identity-based and resource-based permissions form a union; an allow in either can permit the action.; An explicit deny in either an identity-based or resource-based policy overrides an allow.; For a user, identity-based permissions and a permissions boundary form an intersection; adding a boundary can reduce permissions.; For a user in an organization accessing a resource without a resource-based policy, the user's policies, SCPs, and RCP form an intersection. An explicit deny in any of them overrides an allow.
Gotchas: An allow in an identity-based policy does not overcome an explicit deny elsewhere.; A permissions boundary does not grant an action that the user's identity-based policy does not allow.; Do not apply the same-account identity/resource-policy union rule to every combination of policy types.
Confused with: 
ES: IAM evalúa las políticas aplicables a una solicitud, y un explicit deny prevalece sobre cualquier allow. En un escenario de examen, identifica los tipos de políticas involucrados antes de decidir si los permisos se combinan por unión o intersección.
