El aislamiento de fallas limita el impacto de una falla a un límite definido.; Ejecutar una carga de trabajo en varios límites de aislamiento puede mejorar su resiliencia.; La guía de confiabilidad de AWS recomienda implementar las cargas de trabajo en varias ubicaciones.; Para componentes restringidos a una sola ubicación, la guía recomienda automatizar la recuperación.; Una arquitectura bulkhead limita el alcance del impacto, pero por sí sola no distribuye la carga de trabajo entre varias ubicaciones.

chunks.title: Multi-AZ high availability design
chunks.text:
Scenario: A small manufacturer is redesigning an order portal that uses EC2 application instances and an Amazon RDS database. It must accept orders during the loss of either AZ, and the team cannot perform a manual recovery during the outage. Which TWO actions together meet these requirements? (Choose two.)
Correct: Run application instances in an Auto Scaling group across both AZs behind a load balancer that selects healthy targets. + Use an RDS Multi-AZ deployment so the database tier has a failover location in the other AZ.
Why: Accepting orders requires both the application and database tiers, so protecting only one tier is insufficient. The application instances need healthy capacity and traffic routing across AZs, while the database needs a failover location. Single-AZ replacement, a manual procedure, and processing isolation each leave a stated AZ-outage or hands-off recovery requirement unmet.
Wrong options: Keep RDS in one AZ and prepare a documented procedure to restore service in the other AZ. (The database still depends on one AZ and recovery requires manual action.); Run all application instances in one AZ with an Auto Scaling group configured to replace unhealthy instances there. (Instance replacement in one AZ does not keep the application tier available if that AZ is lost.); Divide order requests into isolated processing groups while leaving the application and database in one AZ. (Processing isolation does not remove either tier’s dependency on that AZ.)

chunks.title: Multi-AZ high availability design
chunks.text:
Scenario: A museum runs a stateless visitor-information service on EC2 instances in two AZs. An Application Load Balancer fronts the service, but the proposed configuration continues sending requests to registered instances even when they cannot serve pages. Visitors must receive responses from the surviving AZ during an AZ outage. Which change BEST meets this requirement?
Correct: Configure the load balancer to send requests only to healthy targets, and maintain service capacity in both AZs.
Why: The service already spans two AZs; the gap is directing requests away from targets that cannot respond. Health-aware routing, together with capacity in both locations, lets the surviving AZ serve visitors. Merely adding primary-AZ capacity or isolating processing groups does not fix the stated routing problem.
Wrong options: Increase EC2 capacity in the primary AZ and keep the second AZ for manually launched replacements. (More capacity in the failed AZ cannot serve visitors, and launching replacements is manual.); Keep instances in both AZs, but require an operator to remove failed targets from the load balancer. (Visitors can continue to be sent to failed targets until an operator intervenes.); Separate visitor requests into independent processing groups while keeping the current target-routing behavior. (Limiting the scope of a processing failure does not correct routing to unhealthy targets.)

chunks.title: Multi-AZ high availability design
chunks.text:
Scenario: A regional courier service has an EC2-based dispatch API behind a load balancer and an Amazon RDS database. A proposal spreads the API instances across two AZs but keeps RDS in one AZ, relying on automated instance replacement for recovery. Dispatch must remain usable if either AZ is lost. Which revision BEST meets the requirement?
Correct: Move RDS to a Multi-AZ deployment and retain healthy API capacity and health-aware load balancing across both AZs.
Why: Dispatch depends on both the API and the database, so each required tier must remain available when an AZ is lost. The proposed API distribution solves only part of that problem; the revision also removes the database’s single-AZ placement. Automated replacement of API instances and isolation between jobs do not compensate for an unavailable database AZ.
Wrong options: Keep the current placement and divide dispatch jobs into groups that cannot affect one another. (Job isolation does not make the single-AZ database available after that AZ is lost.); Move all API instances into the database AZ and automate replacement of failed API instances there. (Both tiers would then depend on the same AZ remaining available.); Keep RDS in one AZ and add more API instances in the other AZ. (Extra API instances cannot remove the database’s single-AZ dependency.)

chunks.title: Multi-Region architectures
chunks.text:
Multi-Region architectures. Use a multi-Region architecture when the business must continue serving users after its primary Region becomes unavailable, or when serving users from multiple Regions is a stated latency requirement. The decision is whether the requirement justifies placing application compute and data in more than one Region and planning how users reach the appropriate regional endpoint.
When to use: The workload must remain available if its primary Region cannot serve it.; A disaster recovery plan must meet stated recovery time objective (RTO) and recovery point objective (RPO) requirements.; Users in distant locations must be served by regional deployments rather than one central deployment.
Key facts: A disaster is an event that prevents a workload from meeting its business objectives in its primary deployed location.; RTO and RPO are business requirements that guide the disaster recovery approach.; A regional recovery design must account for application compute, usable data, and a way to direct users to the regional endpoint.; Resources placed only in one Region do not provide an application deployment in another Region.
Gotchas: Changing DNS cannot restore service if the destination Region has no application deployment or usable data.; A second copy of data alone does not provide application compute in the second Region.; Do not add a second Region solely for a requirement that concerns disruption within one Region.
Confused with: 
ES: Usa una arquitectura multi-Region cuando el negocio deba seguir atendiendo usuarios si la Region principal deja de estar disponible, o cuando atenderlos desde varias Regions sea un requisito de latencia. La decisión es si ese requisito justifica ubicar cómputo y datos en más de una Region y planificar cómo llegarán los usuarios al endpoint adecuado. Un desastre es un evento que impide que una carga de trabajo cumpla sus objetivos de negocio en su ubicación principal.; RTO y RPO son requisitos de negocio que orientan el enfoque de recuperación ante desastres.; Un diseño de recuperación regional debe contemplar cómputo, datos utilizables y una forma de dirigir a los usuarios al endpoint regional.; Los recursos ubicados solo en una Region no constituyen una implementación de la aplicación en otra Region.

chunks.title: Multi-Region architectures
chunks.text:
Scenario: A regional ticketing company runs an application in one AWS Region. Its continuity requirement covers an interruption in one Availability Zone; it does not require service during an outage of the entire Region. Which architecture meets these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?
Correct: Run the application across multiple Availability Zones in its current Region.
Why: The deciding boundary is one Availability Zone, not the entire Region. Placing the application across Availability Zones addresses that requirement without taking on a second regional deployment. A remote data copy or another DNS record cannot replace application compute when the only deployed Availability Zone is unavailable.
Wrong options: Keep the application in one Availability Zone and add a second Route 53 DNS record. (Another DNS record does not provide an application deployment outside the interrupted Availability Zone.); Keep the application in one Availability Zone and copy its data to another Region. (A remote data copy does not keep application compute available when its only Availability Zone is interrupted.); Run the application in a second Region and direct all users there with Route 53. (A second regional deployment adds scope when the stated requirement concerns one Availability Zone.)

chunks.title: Multi-Region architectures
chunks.text:
Scenario: A healthcare scheduling team is planning disaster recovery for an application deployed in one AWS Region. The business requires the application to serve users from another Region if the primary Region becomes unavailable, using application data available in that recovery Region. Which TWO additions together address the regional recovery requirement? (Choose two.)
Correct: Prepare application compute in a second Region to serve requests there. + Make application data available in the second Region and plan to direct users to its endpoint.
Why: The stated disaster recovery location is a different Region, so the plan needs an application deployment there. It also needs usable data in that Region and a way to direct users to the recovery endpoint. Options B and E provide those complementary parts. Another Availability Zone, primary-Region-only backups, or a DNS record pointing at the original endpoint does not complete regional recovery.
Wrong options: Keep backups for restoring the application only within the primary Region. (A recovery plan confined to the primary Region does not establish service from another Region.); Add another Route 53 record that points to the existing application endpoint in the primary Region. (The new record still points to an endpoint in the Region that may be unavailable.); Add application compute in another Availability Zone of the primary Region. (Another Availability Zone in the primary Region is not a deployment in the required recovery Region.)

chunks.title: Multi-tier (web/app/data) architecture design
chunks.text:
Multi-tier (web/app/data) architecture design. A three-tier application separates presentation, business logic, and data so each layer has a clear role. For a requirement to scale without managing servers, choose the documented serverless pattern: S3 and CloudFront for the website, API Gateway and Lambda for the backend, and DynamoDB for application data.
When to use: A website or mobile app needs distinct presentation, business logic, and data tiers.; The team wants to avoid provisioning and managing servers as demand grows.; Static website assets need faster distribution through a CDN.
Key facts: Amazon S3 can host website assets; CloudFront can distribute S3 assets through a CDN.; API Gateway provides a REST or WebSocket API front door; Lambda runs business logic without the team managing servers.; DynamoDB is a serverless NoSQL data tier that can store application data and track transactions.; Serverless services offer automatic scaling and built-in high availability.
Gotchas: A CDN improves asset distribution; it does not replace the business logic tier.; An API front door alone does not supply application code when the scenario requires business logic.; Do not select a database solely because it can store data; check whether the requirement calls for a serverless NoSQL data tier.
Confused with: 
ES: Una aplicación de tres capas separa presentación, lógica de negocio y datos para que cada capa tenga una función clara. Si necesitas escalar sin administrar servidores, elige el patrón serverless documentado: S3 y CloudFront para el sitio, API Gateway y Lambda para el backend, y DynamoDB para los datos. Amazon S3 puede alojar recursos del sitio; CloudFront puede distribuirlos mediante un CDN.; API Gateway proporciona la entrada para una API REST o WebSocket; Lambda ejecuta la lógica de negocio sin que administres servidores.; DynamoDB es una capa de datos NoSQL serverless que puede almacenar datos de la aplicación y registrar transacciones.; Los servicios serverless ofrecen escalado automático y alta disponibilidad integrada.

chunks.title: Multi-tier (web/app/data) architecture design
chunks.text:
Scenario: A neighborhood marketplace is launching a website with product listings and customer actions. It needs a CDN for website assets, an API that runs business logic, and a serverless NoSQL store for application data. Which architecture meets these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?
Correct: Use S3 and CloudFront for the website, API Gateway and Lambda for actions, and DynamoDB for data.
Why: The requirement identifies a job for each tier: CDN-backed presentation, API-based business logic, and serverless NoSQL storage. S3 with CloudFront, API Gateway with Lambda, and DynamoDB match those jobs. Omitting CloudFront loses the requested CDN; omitting Lambda leaves out the component that runs the business logic. Amazon RDS does not meet the stated DynamoDB-style serverless NoSQL requirement.
Wrong options: Use S3 and CloudFront for the website, API Gateway and Lambda for actions, and Amazon RDS for data. (This does not select the specified serverless NoSQL data tier.); Use S3 and CloudFront for the website, API Gateway for actions, and DynamoDB for data. (This omits the Lambda functions needed to run the stated business logic.); Use S3 for the website, API Gateway and Lambda for actions, and DynamoDB for data. (This omits CloudFront, so it does not meet the stated CDN requirement.)

chunks.title: Multi-tier (web/app/data) architecture design
chunks.text:
Scenario: A field-service company already has a mobile interface but must add a REST API for scheduling requests. Each request needs application code to apply scheduling rules and then store records in a serverless NoSQL database. The company does not want to provision servers for the new backend. Which solution meets these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?
Correct: Use API Gateway for the REST API, Lambda for scheduling rules, and DynamoDB for records.
Why: A REST front door, executable scheduling logic, and a serverless NoSQL data tier are all explicit requirements. API Gateway, Lambda, and DynamoDB fill those roles without requiring the company to provision backend servers. The EC2 alternative misses that operational constraint, while CloudFront addresses asset distribution rather than the requested API front door. The RDS alternative misses the specified NoSQL data requirement.
Wrong options: Use API Gateway for the REST API, Amazon EC2 for scheduling rules, and DynamoDB for records. (EC2 introduces servers to provision for the backend, contrary to the stated constraint.); Use API Gateway for the REST API, Lambda for scheduling rules, and Amazon RDS for records. (Amazon RDS does not satisfy the specified serverless NoSQL database requirement.); Use CloudFront for requests, Lambda for scheduling rules, and DynamoDB for records. (CloudFront serves the CDN role rather than the required REST API front door.)

chunks.title: Multi-tier (web/app/data) architecture design
chunks.text:
Scenario: An online language school already uses API Gateway, Lambda, and DynamoDB for enrollment requests. It is adding a website with downloadable assets and user sign-in. The website assets must be distributed through a CDN, and the team wants a managed way to authenticate users. Which addition meets these requirements?
Correct: Host assets on S3, distribute them with CloudFront, and use Cognito user pools for sign-in.
Why: The existing API, logic, and data tiers do not need replacing; the new requirements concern website presentation and authentication. S3 can host the assets, CloudFront can distribute them through a CDN, and Cognito user pools can authenticate users. Options without CloudFront miss the explicit CDN requirement. Using Lambda instead of Cognito user pools does not select the documented managed user-authentication component.
Wrong options: Host assets on S3, use API Gateway for sign-in, and use Cognito user pools for users. (This does not add CloudFront to distribute the assets through a CDN.); Host assets on S3, distribute them with CloudFront, and use Lambda for sign-in. (This omits Cognito user pools, the documented managed service for authenticating users.); Host assets on S3, use Cognito user pools for sign-in, and send requests to the existing API. (This provides hosting and authentication but omits the required CDN.)

chunks.title: Multi-tier VPC architecture across AZs
chunks.text:
Multi-tier VPC architecture across AZs. Place the internet-facing load balancer in public subnets and application servers in private subnets across at least two Availability Zones. Keep internal tiers private, use security-group references to restrict tier-to-tier traffic, and choose routes based on whether traffic stays inside the VPC or needs outbound internet access.
When to use: A public application must remain available if one Availability Zone fails.; Application or data servers must not receive direct internet traffic.; Private servers need outbound internet access without being placed in public subnets.
Key facts: The documented resilient VPC example uses public and private subnets in two Availability Zones, with an Application Load Balancer in the public subnets and Auto Scaling servers in the private subnets.; Public subnet route tables have a route to an internet gateway; private subnet route tables retain local routes for VPC traffic.; Private servers can use NAT gateways for outbound internet access; the example places one NAT gateway in each Availability Zone for resiliency.; A server security group must allow traffic from the load balancer security group on the backend target port and health-check port.; A gateway VPC endpoint can provide private-subnet access to Amazon S3.
Gotchas: Putting servers in public subnets is not necessary just because users reach the application through a public load balancer.; A NAT gateway supports outbound internet access from private servers; it does not replace the load balancer's inbound path.; Do not send traffic between tiers in the same VPC through a NAT gateway or internet gateway when local routing applies.; Allowing the load balancer's application port but omitting its distinct health-check port can break health checks.
Confused with: 
ES: Ubica el load balancer expuesto a internet en subredes públicas y los servidores de aplicación en subredes privadas de al menos dos Availability Zones. Mantén privadas las capas internas, usa referencias a security groups para limitar el tráfico entre capas y elige las rutas según si el tráfico permanece en la VPC o necesita salir a internet. El ejemplo documentado de una VPC resiliente usa subredes públicas y privadas en dos Availability Zones, con un Application Load Balancer en las públicas y servidores de Auto Scaling en las privadas.; Las tablas de rutas de subredes públicas incluyen una ruta hacia un internet gateway; las de subredes privadas conservan rutas locales para el tráfico de la VPC.; Los servidores privados pueden usar NAT gateways para salir a internet; el ejemplo coloca uno en cada Availability Zone para mejorar la resiliencia.; El security group de los servidores debe permitir tráfico desde el security group del load balancer en el puerto de destino del backend y en el puerto de comprobación de estado.; Un gateway VPC endpoint puede dar acceso a Amazon S3 desde subredes privadas.

chunks.title: Multi-tier VPC architecture across AZs
chunks.text:
Scenario: A healthcare portal serves users through an Application Load Balancer in public subnets. Its application instances run in private subnets in two Availability Zones; the load balancer uses a separate health-check port, and the instances need outbound internet access for updates. The team is reviewing changes that must preserve the private application tier and avoid a single-AZ dependency for outbound access. Which TWO changes meet these requirements? (Choose two.)
Correct: Allow the load balancer security group into the instance security group on both the application port and the health-check port. + Deploy a NAT gateway in a public subnet in each Availability Zone and route private-subnet outbound internet traffic through the gateway in the corresponding Availability Zone.
Why: Two separate requirements decide the answer: accept both types of load-balancer traffic and provide resilient outbound internet access without moving instances out of private subnets. The instance security group must allow the load balancer's application and separate health-check ports, and the documented resilient NAT pattern uses a gateway in each Availability Zone. A single NAT gateway misses the outbound resilience requirement, while public application subnets miss the privacy requirement.
Wrong options: Deploy one NAT gateway in a public subnet in either Availability Zone and route both private subnet tiers through it. (A single NAT gateway does not avoid the specified single-AZ dependency for outbound access.); Allow the load balancer security group on the application port only and use the public subnet's internet-gateway route for health checks. (The instances' security group must also allow load-balancer health-check traffic on its required port.); Move the application instances into the public subnets and permit only the load balancer security group as an inbound source. (This violates the requirement to preserve the private application tier.)

chunks.title: Multi-tier VPC architecture across AZs
chunks.text:
Scenario: A ticketing company is moving a customer-facing application into a VPC. Customers must reach the service over the internet, but application instances must not receive direct internet traffic. The application must continue serving requests if one Availability Zone fails. Which design meets these requirements while keeping the application tier private?
Correct: Place an Application Load Balancer in public subnets across two Availability Zones and an Auto Scaling group in private subnets across both; allow the instances to receive the load balancer's application and health-check traffic.
Why: The deciding constraints are a public entry point, private application instances, and resilience across two Availability Zones. An Application Load Balancer in public subnets can send requests to Auto Scaling instances in private subnets, whose security group permits the required application and health-check traffic. NAT gateways address outbound traffic from private servers, so they cannot substitute for the inbound load balancer.
Wrong options: Place the Application Load Balancer in a public subnet in one Availability Zone and the Auto Scaling group in private subnets across two Availability Zones. (The public entry-point design does not span both Availability Zones as required.); Place the Auto Scaling group in private subnets across two Availability Zones and route customer requests through NAT gateways in the corresponding public subnets. (NAT gateways provide outbound internet connectivity for private servers, not the required inbound load-balanced entry point.); Place an Application Load Balancer and the Auto Scaling group in public subnets across two Availability Zones; restrict instance traffic with security groups. (This places the application tier in public subnets despite the requirement to keep it private.)

chunks.title: Multi-tier VPC architecture across AZs
chunks.text:
Scenario: A logistics platform separates its web-facing load balancer, application servers, and data servers into subnet tiers across two Availability Zones. Only the load balancer should initiate requests to the application tier; only the application tier should initiate requests to the data tier. Both server tiers must remain private. Which access design MOST closely matches these requirements?
Correct: Keep both server tiers in private subnets; allow the load balancer security group into the application security group and the application security group into the data security group on required ports.
Why: The requirement is segmentation by both subnet placement and permitted source tier. Keeping the servers private and referencing the preceding tier's security group limits application access to the load balancer and data access to the application tier. Allowing the load balancer into the data tier skips the required boundary, while NAT gateways are for outbound internet access rather than local tier-to-tier routing.
Wrong options: Keep both server tiers in private subnets; allow the load balancer security group into the application tier and route application-to-data traffic through the NAT gateways. (Traffic between these VPC tiers uses local routing rather than an outbound internet path through NAT gateways.); Keep both server tiers in private subnets; allow the load balancer security group into both the application and data security groups. (This permits the load balancer to initiate traffic to the data tier rather than limiting that tier to application-server sources.); Place the application and data servers in public subnets; use security groups to allow only the intended source tiers. (The server tiers would occupy public subnets rather than remaining in private subnets.)

chunks.title: Choosing a database engine (MySQL vs PostgreSQL vs commercial)
chunks.text:
Choosing a database engine (MySQL vs PostgreSQL vs commercial). Choose the database engine that preserves the application's required compatibility: MySQL clients and applications point to RDS for MySQL; PostgreSQL clients and required supported extensions point to RDS for PostgreSQL. Then choose deployment features such as Multi-AZ or read replicas according to the stated requirement.
When to use: An existing application must keep using standard MySQL utilities and applications.; A workload depends on PostgreSQL clients or an extension confirmed as supported by RDS for PostgreSQL.; The team wants a managed relational database with backups, restores, or replicas.
Key facts: RDS for MySQL supports standard MySQL utilities and applications, Multi-AZ deployments, read replicas, backups, and point-in-time restores.; RDS for PostgreSQL supports standard PostgreSQL clients, Multi-AZ deployments, read replicas, backups, and point-in-time restores.; RDS for PostgreSQL provides supported extensions; check that a required extension is supported before selecting it.; RDS does not provide direct SSH or other host access to MySQL or PostgreSQL DB instances.
Gotchas: Do not change engines merely because both support Multi-AZ or read replicas; application compatibility still matters.; Do not treat a read replica as a substitute for the documented Multi-AZ high-availability option for RDS for MySQL.; Do not assume every PostgreSQL extension is available on RDS or that RDS provides host-level control.
Confused with: RDS for MySQL: Choose it when the application must retain MySQL utilities and application compatibility, not PostgreSQL-specific requirements.; Self-managed database: RDS reduces database-management work but does not meet a requirement for direct host access.
ES: Elige el motor que conserve la compatibilidad requerida por la aplicación: las aplicaciones y herramientas MySQL apuntan a RDS for MySQL; los clientes PostgreSQL y las extensiones compatibles requeridas apuntan a RDS for PostgreSQL. Después, elige funciones de implementación como Multi-AZ o read replicas según el requisito. RDS for MySQL admite herramientas y aplicaciones MySQL estándar, implementaciones Multi-AZ, read replicas, respaldos y point-in-time restores.; RDS for PostgreSQL admite clientes PostgreSQL estándar, implementaciones Multi-AZ, read replicas, respaldos y point-in-time restores.; RDS for PostgreSQL ofrece extensiones compatibles; verifica que una extensión requerida sea compatible antes de elegirla.; RDS no proporciona acceso directo por SSH ni otro acceso al host de las instancias de base de datos MySQL o PostgreSQL.

chunks.title: Choosing a database engine (MySQL vs PostgreSQL vs commercial)
chunks.text:
Scenario: A ticketing company is moving an existing MySQL application to AWS without changing its database clients or application queries. The team wants AWS to manage the database and needs a high-availability failover solution, not additional read capacity. Which solution meets these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?
Correct: Deploy RDS for MySQL with a Multi-AZ deployment.
Why: Keeping the existing MySQL clients and queries makes MySQL compatibility decisive. RDS for MySQL supports standard MySQL applications and provides Multi-AZ as a high-availability failover solution. A PostgreSQL deployment changes the engine, while a self-managed MySQL deployment adds operational work. A read replica does not replace the documented Multi-AZ choice for this stated failover requirement.
Wrong options: Deploy RDS for PostgreSQL with a Multi-AZ deployment. (Multi-AZ addresses availability, but PostgreSQL does not preserve the application's stated MySQL compatibility.); Deploy RDS for MySQL with a read replica instead of Multi-AZ. (The stated need is high-availability failover, for which the RDS for MySQL documentation identifies Multi-AZ.); Run MySQL on Amazon EC2 and manage a secondary database server. (It preserves the engine but makes the team manage the database and secondary server.)

chunks.title: Choosing a database engine (MySQL vs PostgreSQL vs commercial)
chunks.text:
Scenario: A publisher is migrating a PostgreSQL application whose support staff use pgAdmin to run SQL commands. The database must run inside a VPC, support point-in-time restores, and require no direct host administration. Which solution meets these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?
Correct: Deploy RDS for PostgreSQL in the VPC and use its point-in-time restore capability.
Why: The existing PostgreSQL application and pgAdmin workflow favor keeping PostgreSQL. RDS for PostgreSQL supports standard SQL clients including pgAdmin, VPC deployment, and point-in-time restores. It also avoids direct host administration because RDS does not provide host access. RDS for MySQL changes the engine, while the EC2 choices add the host-management work the publisher wants to avoid.
Wrong options: Run PostgreSQL on Amazon EC2 in the VPC and administer its backups. (It retains PostgreSQL but adds direct database-host and backup administration that the team wants to avoid.); Deploy RDS for MySQL in the VPC and use its point-in-time restore capability. (It meets the VPC and restore requirements but changes the PostgreSQL engine used by the existing application.); Run MySQL on Amazon EC2 in the VPC and administer its backups. (It changes the required engine and adds database-host administration.)

chunks.title: Reducing NAT gateway charges with VPC endpoints
chunks.text:
Reducing NAT gateway charges with VPC endpoints. Gateway VPC endpoints route traffic to Amazon S3 and DynamoDB without a NAT device and have no additional charge. When private-subnet traffic to these services drives NAT processing charges, associate the relevant route tables with gateway endpoints while keeping NAT routes for destinations that still need them.
When to use: Private-subnet workloads send substantial traffic to S3 or DynamoDB in the same Region.; The goal is to reduce NAT data-processing charges without adding a charge for the endpoint.; Workloads must keep using NAT for destinations other than S3 and DynamoDB.
Key facts: A NAT gateway incurs charges for each hour it is available and each gigabyte it processes.; Gateway endpoints for S3 and DynamoDB have no additional charge.; Creating a gateway endpoint adds a service-prefix-list route to each selected route table; subnets using unassociated route tables do not use that endpoint.; The endpoint route takes precedence over a 0.0.0.0/0 route for the service in the current Region, but the default route still serves other destinations.; A gateway endpoint's prefix list is Region-specific; a route specifying the service's exact IP address range can take precedence over the endpoint route.
Gotchas: Creating an endpoint is not enough if the workload's subnet route table is not associated with it.; Replacing the default route with an endpoint route would not preserve access to unrelated destinations.; A gateway endpoint does not capture traffic to the service in a different Region.; A more-specific route for the service can override the gateway endpoint route.
Confused with: NAT gateway: It can serve other outbound destinations, but it incurs hourly and per-gigabyte processing charges.; Interface VPC endpoint: S3 and DynamoDB support both types; the gateway endpoint is the option documented here as having no additional charge.
ES: Los gateway VPC endpoints enrutan tráfico hacia Amazon S3 y DynamoDB sin un dispositivo NAT y no tienen un cargo adicional. Si el tráfico de subredes privadas hacia esos servicios eleva los cargos de procesamiento de NAT, asocia las tablas de rutas pertinentes con gateway endpoints y conserva las rutas NAT para los demás destinos. Un NAT gateway genera cargos por cada hora que está disponible y por cada gigabyte que procesa.; Los gateway endpoints para S3 y DynamoDB no tienen un cargo adicional.; Al crear un gateway endpoint, se agrega una ruta con la lista de prefijos del servicio a cada tabla de rutas seleccionada; las subredes cuyas tablas no están asociadas no usan ese endpoint.; La ruta del endpoint prevalece sobre una ruta 0.0.0.0/0 para el servicio en la Región actual, pero la ruta predeterminada sigue sirviendo a otros destinos.; La lista de prefijos de un gateway endpoint es específica de una Región; una ruta que indique el rango exacto de direcciones IP del servicio puede prevalecer sobre la ruta del endpoint.

chunks.title: Reducing NAT gateway charges with VPC endpoints
chunks.text:
Scenario: A retail application reads a DynamoDB table in its own Region from private subnets. A DynamoDB gateway endpoint is already associated with the route table used by one group of application servers, but servers in another subnet still send DynamoDB traffic through a NAT gateway. Both groups must keep their NAT routes for other outbound traffic. Which change reduces the remaining NAT processing charges with the LEAST operational overhead?
Correct: Associate the affected subnet's route table with the existing DynamoDB gateway endpoint.
Why: A gateway endpoint applies to subnets through their associated route tables. Associating the second subnet's route table with the existing endpoint automatically adds the DynamoDB prefix-list route, so same-Region DynamoDB requests use the endpoint. The NAT default route can stay for other destinations; changing the first group's route table would not fix the second group's traffic.
Wrong options: Replace the affected subnet's NAT default route with a route to the existing DynamoDB gateway endpoint. (This does not preserve the required NAT path for the subnet's other outbound destinations.); Move the affected servers to the subnet whose route table is already associated with the endpoint. (Relocating servers is unnecessary when their current subnet's route table can be associated with the endpoint.); Add a second DynamoDB gateway endpoint route manually to the route table already associated with the endpoint. (That route table already has the endpoint route, and it is not the route table used by the affected servers.)

chunks.title: Reducing NAT gateway charges with VPC endpoints
chunks.text:
Scenario: A subscription service runs application servers in private subnets. The servers make frequent requests to S3 and DynamoDB in the same Region through a NAT gateway, but they also call a third-party payment API. The architecture team wants to reduce NAT processing charges for both AWS services, use endpoints with no additional charge, and preserve payment API access. Which two actions should the team take? (Choose two.)
Correct: Create S3 and DynamoDB gateway endpoints and associate both with the application route tables. + Keep the NAT default route for destinations other than same-Region S3 and DynamoDB.
Why: The servers need separate gateway endpoint routes for S3 and DynamoDB, which can coexist in their route tables and carry same-Region service traffic without an additional endpoint charge. The endpoint routes take precedence over the NAT default route for matching traffic. The NAT default route must remain for the payment API; an S3-only endpoint would leave DynamoDB traffic on NAT.
Wrong options: Create S3 and DynamoDB interface endpoints instead of gateway endpoints. (The gateway endpoint type is the documented no-additional-charge choice for these services.); Create only an S3 gateway endpoint and associate it with the application route tables. (DynamoDB traffic would still use the NAT gateway, failing the requirement to reduce processing for both services.); Remove the application route tables' NAT default route after creating the endpoints. (The servers still need their NAT route to reach the third-party payment API.)

chunks.title: Reducing NAT gateway charges with VPC endpoints
chunks.text:
Scenario: A media company runs upload workers in private subnets. They send large files to an S3 bucket in the same Region through a NAT gateway, and they also call an external licensing API through that gateway. The company wants to lower NAT processing charges without losing access to the API. Which solution meets these requirements with the LEAST additional endpoint cost?
Correct: Create an S3 gateway endpoint, associate the workers' route tables, and retain the NAT default route.
Why: The deciding requirements are to move same-Region S3 traffic off the NAT gateway while retaining outbound access to an external API. An S3 gateway endpoint has no additional charge, and its route takes precedence over the NAT default route for matching S3 traffic. Removing the NAT route would break the API path; merely changing the workers' Availability Zone would not eliminate NAT processing of S3 traffic.
Wrong options: Create an S3 gateway endpoint, associate the workers' route tables, and remove the NAT default route. (The workers would lose their existing route to the external licensing API.); Create an S3 interface endpoint and leave the workers' existing NAT default route in place. (Although S3 supports interface endpoints, the documented no-additional-charge endpoint choice for this requirement is a gateway endpoint.); Place the workers in the NAT gateway's Availability Zone and leave their S3 traffic on the NAT route. (This does not remove S3 traffic from the NAT gateway's per-gigabyte processing charges.)

chunks.title: NAT gateway per AZ vs single shared NAT gateway
chunks.text:
NAT gateway per AZ vs single shared NAT gateway. A public NAT gateway lets instances in private subnets initiate internet connections without allowing the internet to initiate connections to them. For a multi-AZ workload, choose a NAT gateway in each AZ when outbound access must remain resilient; consider a shared gateway when reducing the number of gateways matters more than that resilience.
When to use: Production private subnets in multiple AZs need resilient outbound internet access: place a public NAT gateway in each AZ and route each private subnet to its local gateway.; A non-production workload accepts dependence on another AZ's NAT gateway and prioritizes fewer hourly gateway charges: share one gateway.; Substantial traffic would otherwise cross AZs to reach a shared gateway: evaluate a NAT gateway in each AZ.
Key facts: A private subnet can route 0.0.0.0/0 to a public NAT gateway in a public subnet; the public subnet routes internet-bound traffic to an internet gateway.; A private subnet in one AZ can route through a NAT gateway in another AZ, but placing a gateway in each AZ improves resiliency.; NAT gateways incur charges for each hour available and each gigabyte processed.; Keeping resources in the same AZ as their NAT gateway can reduce cross-AZ data transfer charges.; A private NAT gateway serves private-network connectivity use cases, not this outbound-internet design.
Gotchas: A single shared gateway can serve private subnets in multiple AZs, but it leaves their outbound access dependent on the gateway's AZ.; A gateway in each AZ does not provide local outbound access unless each private subnet's route points to the gateway in its AZ.; More gateways increase hourly gateway charges; local routing can reduce cross-AZ transfer charges, so compare the requirements rather than assuming one layout is always cheapest.
Confused with: Private NAT gateway: Use a public NAT gateway for private-subnet outbound internet access; the excerpt uses private NAT gateways for private-network connectivity.; VPC endpoint: An endpoint can be worth evaluating for traffic to supported AWS services, but it does not replace the required general internet route.
ES: Un public NAT gateway permite que las instancias en subredes privadas inicien conexiones a internet sin permitir que internet inicie conexiones hacia ellas. Para una carga en varias AZ, elige un NAT gateway por AZ si la salida debe ser resiliente; considera uno compartido si importa más reducir la cantidad de gateways. Una subred privada puede dirigir 0.0.0.0/0 a un public NAT gateway en una subred pública; la subred pública dirige el tráfico hacia internet a un internet gateway.; Una subred privada de una AZ puede usar un NAT gateway de otra AZ, pero colocar uno en cada AZ mejora la resiliencia.; Los NAT gateways generan cargos por cada hora disponible y por cada gigabyte procesado.; Mantener los recursos en la misma AZ que su NAT gateway puede reducir los cargos por transferencia entre AZ.; Un private NAT gateway sirve para casos de conectividad con redes privadas, no para este diseño de salida a internet.

chunks.title: NAT gateway per AZ vs single shared NAT gateway
chunks.text:
Scenario: A ticketing company runs application instances in private subnets across two AZs. The instances must download updates from internet repositories, and an AZ failure must not make outbound access in the surviving AZ depend on the failed AZ. Which solution meets these requirements while keeping the instances private?
Correct: Place a public NAT gateway in each AZ and route each private subnet's default traffic to the gateway in its own AZ.
Why: The deciding requirement is outbound internet access that remains independent of the other AZ. AWS documents a public NAT gateway for private-subnet internet egress and recommends a gateway in each AZ to improve resiliency. Each private subnet must route to its local gateway; merely provisioning a second gateway does not achieve that routing. A shared gateway leaves one AZ dependent on the other.
Wrong options: Place a private NAT gateway in each AZ and route each private subnet's default traffic to its local gateway for internet access. (The documented internet-egress pattern uses public, not private, NAT gateways.); Place a public NAT gateway in each AZ, but route both private subnets' default traffic to the gateway in the first AZ. (The gateway in the second AZ would not be used by its private subnet.); Place one public NAT gateway in the first AZ and route both private subnets' default traffic to it. (The second AZ's outbound access would depend on a gateway in the first AZ.)

chunks.title: NAT gateway per AZ vs single shared NAT gateway
chunks.text:
Scenario: A retailer operates separate production and development VPCs, each with private subnets in two AZs that need occasional outbound access to public internet hosts. Production must retain outbound access in a surviving AZ after an AZ disruption; development accepts that dependency and seeks to minimize gateway hourly charges. Which TWO configurations meet the respective environments' requirements? (Choose two.)
Correct: In development, deploy one public NAT gateway and route both AZs' private subnets to it. + In production, deploy a public NAT gateway in each AZ and route each private subnet to its local gateway.
Why: Production requires AZ-local outbound internet access, so it needs a public NAT gateway in each AZ with each private subnet routed locally. Development explicitly accepts an AZ dependency and prioritizes fewer hourly gateway charges, making one shared public NAT gateway appropriate. Giving production only one gateway misses its resilience requirement. Giving development two gateways adds a charge for resilience it does not require.
Wrong options: In production, deploy a private NAT gateway in each AZ and route each private subnet to its local gateway for internet access. (The internet-egress requirement calls for public NAT gateways rather than private NAT gateways.); In production, deploy one public NAT gateway and route both AZs' private subnets to it. (Production outbound access in one AZ would depend on a gateway in the other AZ.); In development, deploy a public NAT gateway in each AZ and route each private subnet locally. (The second gateway adds an hourly charge despite development's acceptance of the AZ dependency.)

chunks.title: NAT gateway vs NAT instance
chunks.text:
NAT gateway vs NAT instance. A public NAT gateway lets instances in private subnets initiate internet connections without accepting unsolicited inbound connections. Choose it over a NAT instance when managed operation and availability matter; use a gateway in each Availability Zone when the design must remain zone-independent.
When to use: Private instances must download updates or call external APIs without accepting unsolicited inbound internet connections.; The team wants AWS to manage the NAT component rather than patch and size an instance.; Private subnets in multiple Availability Zones need zone-independent outbound access.
Key facts: A public NAT gateway is created in a public subnet with an Elastic IP address and routes internet-bound traffic through the VPC internet gateway.; NAT gateways are managed by AWS and have redundancy within their Availability Zone; a gateway in each Availability Zone provides a zone-independent architecture.; A NAT instance requires you to handle maintenance and arrange failover between instances.; NAT gateway charges depend on gateway count, usage duration, and data sent through the gateways.; You cannot attach a security group to a NAT gateway, and NAT gateways do not support port forwarding.
Gotchas: A private NAT gateway cannot provide internet access through an internet gateway; the internet gateway drops that traffic.; One public NAT gateway shared across Availability Zones does not provide a zone-independent design.; Replacing a NAT instance's route with a NAT gateway route drops existing connections; they must be re-established.
Confused with: NAT instance: A NAT instance is self-managed and can be customized for port forwarding; a NAT gateway is managed and does not support port forwarding.; VPC endpoint: An endpoint for an AWS service is not a substitute for outbound access to arbitrary internet destinations.
ES: Un public NAT gateway permite que las instancias en subredes privadas inicien conexiones a internet sin aceptar conexiones entrantes no solicitadas. Elígelo en lugar de un NAT instance cuando importen la administración a cargo de AWS y la disponibilidad; usa uno por Availability Zone si necesitas independencia entre zonas. Un public NAT gateway se crea en una subred pública con una Elastic IP y dirige el tráfico hacia internet mediante el internet gateway de la VPC.; AWS administra los NAT gateways, que tienen redundancia dentro de su Availability Zone; uno en cada zona permite una arquitectura independiente por zona.; Con un NAT instance, tú te encargas del mantenimiento y de organizar la conmutación por error entre instancias.; Los cargos de NAT gateway dependen de la cantidad de gateways, el tiempo de uso y los datos enviados a través de ellos.; No puedes asociar un security group a un NAT gateway, y los NAT gateways no admiten port forwarding.

chunks.title: NAT gateway vs NAT instance
chunks.text:
Scenario: A healthcare analytics company runs private-subnet workers in multiple Availability Zones. Workers must reach a third-party internet API without accepting unsolicited inbound internet connections, and outbound access must remain zone-independent. The company wants AWS to manage the NAT components. Which two actions should the company take? (Choose two.)
Correct: Create a public NAT gateway with an Elastic IP in a public subnet in each Availability Zone. + Route each private subnet's internet-bound traffic to the public NAT gateway in its own Availability Zone.
Why: The workers need public-internet egress, not unsolicited inbound access, so the NAT components must be public NAT gateways rather than private ones. Creating a gateway in each Availability Zone and routing each zone's private subnets through their local gateway provides a zone-independent architecture. A shared gateway would introduce the zone dependency the scenario forbids. Security groups cannot be attached to NAT gateways.
Wrong options: Create private NAT gateways and send their outbound traffic through the VPC internet gateway. (The internet gateway drops traffic from private NAT gateways.); Route all private subnets through one public NAT gateway to reduce the number of gateways. (A single gateway does not meet the stated zone-independence requirement.); Attach security groups directly to the NAT gateways to block unsolicited inbound internet traffic. (Security groups cannot be associated directly with NAT gateways.)

chunks.title: NAT gateway vs NAT instance
chunks.text:
Scenario: A media company runs processing workers in private subnets across two Availability Zones. The workers must call an external licensing API, must not accept unsolicited inbound internet connections, and must retain outbound access if either zone fails. Which solution meets these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?
Correct: Deploy one public NAT gateway in each Availability Zone and route each private subnet through the gateway in its own zone.
Why: The external API requires outbound internet access, while the workers must remain protected from unsolicited inbound connections. Public NAT gateways provide that behavior without instance maintenance. A gateway in each Availability Zone meets the zone-independence requirement; sharing one gateway across zones does not.
Wrong options: Deploy one public NAT gateway in one Availability Zone and route both private subnets through it. (A single gateway does not meet the requirement to retain outbound access if its zone fails.); Deploy a NAT instance in each Availability Zone and route each private subnet through its local instance. (NAT instances require instance maintenance and failover management, increasing operational overhead.); Deploy one private NAT gateway in each Availability Zone and route their traffic to the internet gateway. (An internet gateway drops traffic routed to it from a private NAT gateway.)

chunks.title: NAT gateway vs NAT instance
chunks.text:
Scenario: A publisher uses a NAT instance for outbound connections from a private subnet. Its partner allows requests only from the instance's current Elastic IP address, and the publisher wants to move to managed NAT during a scheduled maintenance window. Existing connections can be interrupted during that window. Which migration approach meets these requirements?
Correct: Disassociate the Elastic IP from the NAT instance, associate it with a new public NAT gateway at creation, and replace the private subnet's NAT route.
Why: The partner's allowlist makes reuse of the existing Elastic IP decisive. AWS documents disassociating it from the NAT instance, associating it with the public NAT gateway when the gateway is created, and updating the route. Existing connections are dropped by the change, which the scheduled window permits. A new Elastic IP would fail the partner's allowlist.
Wrong options: Create a private NAT gateway, attach the existing Elastic IP to it, and replace the private subnet's NAT route. (A private NAT gateway cannot have an Elastic IP and cannot provide the required internet egress.); Create a public NAT gateway with a new Elastic IP, change the private route, and keep the old NAT instance's Elastic IP attached. (The partner would see a different Elastic IP address, violating its allowlist requirement.); Keep the NAT instance, update its operating system during maintenance, and leave the private subnet's route unchanged. (Keeping the instance does not meet the requirement to move to managed NAT.)

chunks.title: Amazon Neptune (graph database)
chunks.text:
Amazon Neptune (graph database). Amazon Neptune is a fully managed graph database for applications that navigate highly connected data. Choose it when relationships and graph queries—not just individual records—drive the database decision.
When to use: An application repeatedly traverses connections in a social network, fraud graph, or knowledge graph.; The required query language is Gremlin or openCypher for a property graph, or SPARQL for an RDF graph.; A graph workload needs managed backups and read replicas across Availability Zones.
Key facts: Neptune supports Gremlin and openCypher for property graphs and SPARQL for RDF graphs.; Its engine is optimized for storing billions of relationships and querying graphs with millisecond latency.; A Neptune DB cluster has one primary DB instance for writes and can have up to 15 read-only Neptune Replicas.; Neptune replicates cluster-volume data across multiple Availability Zones within one AWS Region.; Neptune manages tasks including provisioning, patching, configuration, and backups.
Gotchas: A graph-shaped workload is not automatically a good fit for a relational engine just because its entities can be stored in tables.; DynamoDB's key-value and document access patterns do not replace a stated requirement to traverse a graph with Gremlin, openCypher, or SPARQL.; Neptune Replicas serve reads; the primary DB instance performs writes.
Confused with: Amazon DynamoDB: Choose Neptune for graph traversal and graph query languages; choose DynamoDB for key-value or document access patterns.; Amazon DocumentDB: DocumentDB fits MongoDB-compatible document workloads; Neptune fits connected-data graph queries.; Amazon Aurora: Aurora fits MySQL- or PostgreSQL-compatible relational workloads; Neptune is purpose-built for graph relationships.
ES: Amazon Neptune es una base de datos de grafos fully managed para aplicaciones que recorren datos muy conectados. Elígela cuando las relaciones y las consultas de grafos, y no solo los registros individuales, determinen la elección de la base de datos. Neptune admite Gremlin y openCypher para property graphs, y SPARQL para grafos RDF.; Su motor está optimizado para almacenar miles de millones de relaciones y consultar grafos con latencia de milisegundos.; Un Neptune DB cluster tiene una instancia primaria para escrituras y puede tener hasta 15 Neptune Replicas de solo lectura.; Neptune replica los datos del cluster volume entre varias Availability Zones dentro de una AWS Region.; Neptune administra tareas como aprovisionamiento, aplicación de parches, configuración y backups.

chunks.title: Amazon Neptune (graph database)
chunks.text:
Scenario: A payment platform links accounts, devices, and transactions to investigate suspicious activity. Its application must traverse several connections between these entities using Gremlin as each case is reviewed. Which database meets these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?
Correct: Amazon Neptune with a property graph
Why: The deciding requirement is to traverse connected entities using Gremlin. Neptune supports Gremlin for property graphs and is fully managed, so it meets both the query and operational requirements. Storing the entities in DynamoDB, Aurora, or DocumentDB would not provide the specified graph query interface.
Wrong options: Amazon Aurora with relational tables for each entity (Aurora is a relational choice, not the requested Gremlin graph database.); Amazon DocumentDB with a document for each transaction (DocumentDB serves document workloads rather than the required Gremlin graph traversal.); Amazon DynamoDB with account and device items (DynamoDB can store the entities, but it does not satisfy the stated Gremlin graph-query requirement.)

chunks.title: Amazon Neptune (graph database)
chunks.text:
Scenario: A research publisher is building a knowledge graph that links papers, authors, and research topics. Its existing tooling represents the data as RDF and sends SPARQL queries to explore those links. Which managed database should the publisher select to preserve this query approach with the LEAST operational overhead?
Correct: Amazon Neptune with an RDF graph
Why: The existing RDF model and SPARQL queries are the deciding constraints, not merely the presence of papers and authors. Neptune supports RDF graphs through SPARQL and manages database operations. Keyspaces would fit a CQL requirement, while DocumentDB and RDS would not preserve the stated graph-query approach.
Wrong options: Amazon RDS with relational tables for papers and authors (Relational tables do not preserve the application's specified RDF and SPARQL query approach.); Amazon DocumentDB with JSON documents for papers and authors (DocumentDB is a document database and does not meet the stated SPARQL query requirement.); Amazon Keyspaces with CQL queries over wide-column tables (Keyspaces is intended for Cassandra-compatible CQL workloads, not the required RDF and SPARQL approach.)

chunks.title: Network ACLs (stateless subnet firewall)
chunks.text:
Network ACLs (stateless subnet firewall). A network ACL (NACL) controls inbound and outbound traffic at the subnet boundary. Choose it when a scenario requires a subnet-wide rule or an explicit deny, and check both directions because NACLs are stateless.
When to use: Block a specific source IP address or CIDR while allowing other traffic to a subnet.; Apply the same traffic policy to every resource in a subnet.; Troubleshoot replies dropped by a restrictive subnet-level policy.
Key facts: NACL rules can allow or deny traffic and are evaluated from the lowest rule number upward; evaluation stops at the first match.; Inbound and outbound rules are separate. Allowing a request does not automatically allow its response.; Return traffic to a client can require a rule for the client's ephemeral destination ports.; Each subnet has one NACL association at a time; a NACL can be associated with multiple subnets.
Gotchas: An allow rule with a lower number can make a later deny rule ineffective.; A security group cannot express an explicit deny rule.; Opening the request port alone may leave return traffic blocked by a custom NACL.
Confused with: security-groups: Security groups filter at the instance or network-interface level, use allow rules, and automatically permit responses to allowed traffic; NACLs filter at the subnet level and are stateless.
ES: Una network ACL (NACL) controla el tráfico entrante y saliente en el límite de una subred. Elígela cuando necesites una regla para toda la subred o una denegación explícita, y revisa ambas direcciones porque las NACL son stateless. Las reglas de una NACL pueden permitir o denegar tráfico; se evalúan desde el número más bajo y la evaluación termina en la primera coincidencia.; Las reglas entrantes y salientes son independientes. Permitir una solicitud no permite automáticamente su respuesta.; El tráfico de respuesta hacia un cliente puede necesitar una regla para los puertos efímeros de destino del cliente.; Cada subred tiene una sola asociación de NACL a la vez; una NACL puede asociarse con varias subredes.

chunks.title: Network ACLs (stateless subnet firewall)
chunks.text:
Scenario: An analytics company has instances in a private subnet that initiate HTTPS connections to a partner's address range through a NAT gateway. A custom network ACL permits outbound TCP port 443 to the partner, but the instances do not receive responses; their security groups permit the connections. Which change restores the responses while keeping the subnet policy restricted to the partner?
Correct: Allow inbound traffic from the partner's address range to the client ephemeral ports in the subnet's network ACL.
Why: The instances initiate the HTTPS connections, so the missing packets are responses entering their subnet. A stateless NACL needs an inbound rule that permits those packets to the clients' ephemeral ports. An inbound rule for port 443 addresses the wrong destination port, and changing security groups does not fix a NACL drop.
Wrong options: Allow inbound traffic from the partner's address range to client ephemeral ports in the instances' security groups. (Stateful security groups already permit responses to allowed connections and cannot override a NACL block.); Allow inbound TCP port 443 from the partner's address range in the subnet's network ACL. (The response is destined for the initiating client's ephemeral port, not its HTTPS destination port.); Allow outbound client ephemeral ports to the partner's address range in the subnet's network ACL. (This does not permit the missing inbound response traffic.)

chunks.title: Network ACLs (stateless subnet firewall)
chunks.text:
Scenario: A manufacturer allows administrative traffic from a peered VPC into a maintenance subnet. Its subnet network ACL has inbound rule 100 allowing the peered VPC's CIDR, but a smaller range within that CIDR is no longer trusted. The manufacturer must deny that smaller range without interrupting access from the rest of the peered VPC. Which change meets this requirement?
Correct: Add a NACL deny rule for the smaller range with a rule number lower than 100.
Why: The smaller untrusted range is contained within a CIDR already allowed by rule 100. NACL rules are evaluated in ascending number order and evaluation stops at the first match, so its deny must have a number below 100. A later deny is ineffective, while denying the whole peered CIDR would break required access.
Wrong options: Replace NACL rule 100 with a deny rule for the entire peered VPC CIDR. (Denying the entire CIDR would interrupt access from the trusted remainder.); Add a security group deny rule for the smaller range on each maintenance instance. (Security groups have no deny rules.); Add a NACL deny rule for the smaller range with a rule number greater than 100. (Rule 100 would allow matching traffic before the new deny rule is evaluated.)

chunks.title: Network ACLs (stateless subnet firewall)
chunks.text:
Scenario: A community library hosts an HTTPS service on instances in a dedicated subnet. Clients in a known address range initiate connections to TCP port 443, and their responses must reach those clients; the subnet's custom network ACL currently has no applicable allow rules. The instances' security groups already permit the client connections. Which two network ACL rules are needed to permit the request and response traffic? (Choose two.)
Correct: Allow outbound traffic to client ephemeral ports in the client address range. + Allow inbound TCP port 443 from the client address range.
Why: Clients send requests into the subnet on TCP port 443, so the NACL needs an inbound allow for that port. Responses leave the subnet for the clients' ephemeral ports, requiring a separate outbound allow because NACLs are stateless. An outbound port 443 rule targets the wrong destination port, and the existing security group permissions do not replace either NACL rule.
Wrong options: Allow inbound traffic to client ephemeral ports from the client address range. (The incoming client requests are destined for the service's port 443.); Allow outbound TCP port 443 to the client address range. (Replies to client-initiated connections are destined for client ephemeral ports, not port 443.); Allow TCP port 443 from the client address range in the instances' security groups. (That access is already permitted by the security groups and does not create a missing NACL rule.)

chunks.title: Bandwidth allocation: multiple VPNs, ECMP, DX speeds
chunks.text:
Bandwidth allocation: multiple VPNs, ECMP, DX speeds. Size hybrid connectivity against the bandwidth requirement, not just the number of connections. For higher aggregate Site-to-Site VPN bandwidth, use multiple tunnels with ECMP on a transit gateway and dynamic routing; for a dedicated Direct Connect connection, select a sufficient port speed when creating it.
When to use: Traffic must exceed the bandwidth available from one standard VPN tunnel, and multiple tunnels can be used.; A workload requires a dedicated Direct Connect port sized for a stated bandwidth target.; An existing dedicated Direct Connect port is too small for a new requirement.
Key facts: A standard Site-to-Site VPN tunnel supports up to 1.25 Gbps; realized bandwidth depends on traffic and network conditions.; A large bandwidth VPN tunnel supports up to 5 Gbps.; Transit gateway VPN connections can use ECMP to aggregate multiple tunnels, but ECMP requires dynamic routing and does not support static routing.; Dedicated Direct Connect port speeds are 1, 10, 100, and 400 Gbps.; A dedicated Direct Connect port speed cannot be changed after the connection request; a different speed requires a new connection.
Gotchas: Enabling ECMP without switching a statically routed VPN connection to dynamic routing does not meet the ECMP requirement.; Two VPN tunnels do not establish a guaranteed aggregate throughput; the documented tunnel maximums are upper bounds.; A dedicated Direct Connect port cannot be resized in place.
Confused with: Static-routing VPN connections: Transit gateway VPN ECMP requires dynamic routing; static-routing VPN connections cannot use it.; Hosted Direct Connect connections: A hosted connection is requested through a Direct Connect Partner, whereas a dedicated port has a fixed speed after its connection request.
ES: Dimensiona la conectividad híbrida según el ancho de banda requerido, no solo según la cantidad de conexiones. Para aumentar el ancho de banda agregado de Site-to-Site VPN, usa varios túneles con ECMP en un transit gateway y enrutamiento dinámico; para Direct Connect dedicated, elige una velocidad de puerto suficiente al crear la conexión. Un túnel Site-to-Site VPN estándar admite hasta 1,25 Gbps; el ancho de banda real depende del tráfico y de las condiciones de la red.; Un túnel VPN de gran ancho de banda admite hasta 5 Gbps.; Las conexiones VPN en un transit gateway pueden usar ECMP para agregar varios túneles, pero ECMP requiere enrutamiento dinámico y no admite enrutamiento estático.; Las velocidades de puerto de Direct Connect dedicated son 1, 10, 100 y 400 Gbps.; No puedes cambiar la velocidad de un puerto Direct Connect dedicated después de solicitar la conexión; necesitas una conexión nueva.

chunks.title: Bandwidth allocation: multiple VPNs, ECMP, DX speeds
chunks.text:
Scenario: A video production company has two standard Site-to-Site VPN connections attached to a transit gateway. The connections currently use static routing, and the company wants to increase potential aggregate bandwidth beyond the limit of one standard tunnel by using its existing tunnels. Which solution meets these requirements without ordering a new circuit?
Correct: Configure the VPN connections for dynamic routing and use ECMP on the transit gateway.
Why: The deciding requirement is to increase potential aggregate bandwidth using the existing VPN tunnels. Site-to-Site VPN connections on a transit gateway can use ECMP for this purpose when configured for dynamic routing. Keeping static routing prevents ECMP, while using just one connection does not aggregate the tunnels. Actual VPN throughput can still vary with traffic and network conditions.
Wrong options: Replace the VPN connections with a 1 Gbps dedicated Direct Connect connection. (This requires a new circuit and its selected port speed does not exceed the standard VPN tunnel maximum.); Use dynamic routing on one VPN connection and route all production traffic through that connection. (Using only one connection does not aggregate bandwidth across the existing tunnels.); Enable ECMP on the transit gateway and retain static routing for both VPN connections. (Transit gateway VPN ECMP does not support connections that use static routing.)

chunks.title: Bandwidth allocation: multiple VPNs, ECMP, DX speeds
chunks.text:
Scenario: A research institute is planning a dedicated Direct Connect connection for data transfers from its facility. Its network team requires a port speed that accommodates a 6 Gbps target and will request the dedicated connection directly rather than obtain a hosted connection through a partner. Which solution meets these requirements with the LEAST excess provisioned port capacity?
Correct: Request a 10 Gbps dedicated Direct Connect connection.
Why: The institute needs a dedicated port with a speed of at least 6 Gbps and wants the smallest qualifying option. Dedicated Direct Connect port speeds include 1, 10, 100, and 400 Gbps, making 10 Gbps the appropriate selection. A 1 Gbps port is too small; a 100 Gbps port provides more excess capacity. A hosted connection misses the stated dedicated-connection requirement.
Wrong options: Request a 100 Gbps dedicated Direct Connect connection. (It exceeds the target by more than the available 10 Gbps dedicated port.); Request a 10 Gbps hosted Direct Connect connection through a partner. (A hosted connection does not satisfy the requirement to request a dedicated connection directly.); Request a 1 Gbps dedicated Direct Connect connection. (A 1 Gbps port is below the stated 6 Gbps target.)

chunks.title: AWS Network Firewall
chunks.text:
AWS Network Firewall. AWS Network Firewall is a managed, stateful firewall and intrusion prevention service for VPC traffic. Choose it when traffic must pass through inspection for threats, domains, or protocols—not merely be permitted by port and address.
When to use: Inspect VPC traffic entering or leaving through an internet gateway, NAT gateway, VPN, or Direct Connect.; Filter access to domains or apply Suricata-compatible intrusion prevention rules.; Steer traffic from protected subnets through firewall endpoints using VPC route tables.
Key facts: Stateful rules can inspect traffic in the context of its flow; Network Firewall also supports stateless rules.; Stateful inspection supports domain filtering, 5-tuple rules, and Suricata-compatible IPS rules.; Stateful protocol detection can identify HTTPS independently of its port.; In the default source-preservation mode, inspection preserves the original source and destination IP addresses.; A firewall endpoint cannot filter traffic entering or leaving its own subnet; reserve firewall subnets for Network Firewall.
Gotchas: Creating a firewall is not enough: VPC route tables must direct the relevant traffic through its endpoints.; Do not place protected workloads in a firewall subnet.; Routing traffic through an endpoint in another Availability Zone can incur cross-zone traffic charges.
Confused with: AWS Firewall Manager: Firewall Manager centrally configures and manages firewalls across accounts; Network Firewall performs the VPC traffic filtering.; AWS WAF: WAF protects supported web application entry points; Network Firewall inspects traffic routed through its VPC endpoints.
ES: AWS Network Firewall es un firewall administrado con inspección stateful y prevención de intrusiones para tráfico de VPC. Elígelo cuando debas inspeccionar amenazas, dominios o protocolos en el tráfico, no solo permitir conexiones según puertos y direcciones. Las reglas stateful inspeccionan paquetes en el contexto de su flujo; Network Firewall también admite reglas stateless.; La inspección stateful admite filtrado de dominios, reglas de 5 tuplas y reglas IPS compatibles con Suricata.; La detección stateful puede identificar HTTPS independientemente del puerto.; En el modo predeterminado source-preservation, la inspección conserva las direcciones IP originales de origen y destino.; Un endpoint del firewall no puede filtrar tráfico que entra o sale de su propia subred; reserva las subredes del firewall para Network Firewall.

chunks.title: AWS Network Firewall
chunks.text:
Scenario: A publisher's private-subnet workers download content through a NAT gateway. The security team has a changing list of malicious domains and wants to inspect outbound flows with intrusion prevention rules before they leave the VPC. Which solution meets these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?
Correct: Deploy AWS Network Firewall with stateful domain and IPS rules, and route the workers' outbound traffic through its endpoints.
Why: The deciding requirement is to filter destination domains and apply IPS rules to outbound VPC traffic before it exits through the NAT gateway. Network Firewall supports both rule types, and VPC routes steer traffic to its endpoints. Firewall Manager can centrally manage firewall deployments, but security group policies based on ports do not replace the requested inspection.
Wrong options: Use AWS Firewall Manager to distribute security group policies that permit only the workers' required outbound ports. (Port-based security group policies do not provide the requested domain filtering and intrusion prevention inspection.); Use Amazon GuardDuty to identify suspicious worker activity and send findings to the security team. (Threat findings do not filter the specified outbound flows before they leave the VPC.); Attach an AWS WAF web ACL to the publisher's public application and add rules for suspicious requests. (Protecting the public web application does not inspect the workers' outbound traffic through the NAT gateway.)

chunks.title: AWS Network Firewall
chunks.text:
Scenario: A manufacturer connects an on-premises network to a VPC over VPN. Its security policy requires stateful inspection of traffic arriving over the VPN and detection of HTTPS even when applications use an unexpected port. The inspected traffic must retain its original source and destination IP addresses. Which solution meets these requirements?
Correct: Route the VPN traffic through AWS Network Firewall endpoints using its default source-preservation mode and stateful protocol rules.
Why: The key constraint is protocol-aware, stateful inspection of VPN traffic without changing its original IP addresses. Network Firewall supports filtering traffic over VPN and detecting HTTPS independently of port; its default source-preservation mode retains the original addresses. Network ACLs and security group rules based on expected ports miss the unexpected-port requirement.
Wrong options: Use AWS Firewall Manager to centrally apply security group rules for the VPN traffic. (Centralized security group rules do not perform stateful HTTPS protocol detection independent of port.); Configure network ACL rules for the expected HTTPS port on the protected subnets. (Port-based network ACL rules cannot meet the requirement to detect HTTPS on an unexpected port.); Enable Amazon GuardDuty and review findings for suspicious traffic associated with the VPC. (Reviewing threat findings does not provide the required in-path protocol inspection.)

chunks.title: Reviewing existing workloads for network optimizations
chunks.text:
Reviewing existing workloads for network optimizations. Review an existing workload’s traffic patterns and network costs before changing its topology. Use the findings to decide whether to co-locate frequently communicating components, remove unnecessary hops, or consolidate network resources without breaking required connectivity or availability.
When to use: A workload’s network costs have increased, but the costly traffic paths are not yet clear.; Components communicate frequently through NAT gateways or Transit Gateway attachments.; A team wants to simplify an existing network while preserving its routing and availability requirements.
Key facts: Cloud networking resources are consumed and paid for as they are used.; Efficient use of networking resources is part of cost optimization.; AWS cost-optimization guidance recommends modeling data transfer before making changes.; The guidance also recommends selecting components and implementing services to reduce data transfer costs.
Gotchas: Do not consolidate network resources solely because the diagram looks complicated; check traffic and cost data first.; Removing a hop is not an optimization if that hop provides required connectivity.; Moving components closer together must not violate the workload’s availability requirements.
Confused with: 
ES: Revisa los patrones de tráfico y los costos de red de una carga de trabajo existente antes de cambiar su topología. Usa los resultados para decidir si conviene acercar componentes que se comunican con frecuencia, eliminar saltos innecesarios o consolidar recursos de red sin afectar la conectividad ni la disponibilidad requeridas. Los recursos de red en la nube se consumen y se pagan según su uso.; El uso eficiente de los recursos de red forma parte de la optimización de costos.; La guía de optimización de costos de AWS recomienda modelar la transferencia de datos antes de hacer cambios.; La guía también recomienda seleccionar componentes e implementar servicios que reduzcan los costos de transferencia de datos.

chunks.title: Reviewing existing workloads for network optimizations
chunks.text:
Scenario: A retailer runs applications across several VPCs. Its network spending has increased, and engineers suspect that some application-to-application traffic takes unnecessary paths through shared network resources, but they have not identified the traffic sources. The team must keep existing connectivity while deciding what to change. Which approach meets these requirements MOST cost-effectively?
Correct: Review VPC Flow Logs and AWS Cost Explorer data, model the significant traffic paths, and then change only paths shown to be unnecessary.
Why: The deciding constraint is that the team has not identified which paths drive spending and must preserve connectivity. Reviewing traffic and cost data supports data transfer modeling before selecting changes. Removing attachments immediately may disrupt required connections, while adding resources or migrating everything makes unverified changes to the topology.
Wrong options: Remove the shared AWS Transit Gateway attachments first, then investigate any application connections that stop working. (Removing attachments before identifying required paths risks breaking existing connectivity.); Add NAT gateways to each VPC first, then compare network spending after the deployment. (Adding resources before identifying the costly paths does not target the stated problem.); Move every application component into one VPC first, then inspect traffic that still crosses network boundaries. (A broad migration is not justified before the team knows which paths need optimization.)

chunks.title: Reviewing existing workloads for network optimizations
chunks.text:
Scenario: A media company operates a processing service and a metadata service in separate locations within its AWS network. A review of VPC Flow Logs shows frequent communication between the two, and the team wants to reduce avoidable data transfer while retaining the workload’s required availability.
